triage.name: Pawn Forfeiture Flow Meter
triage.data_exists: Yes. shop.ezpawn.com is live, public, Shopify-powered (footer says 'Powered by Shopify', images on Shopify CDN), with Electronics/Jewelry/Tools/Gaming/Smart Watches/Music collections pooling inventory from 500+ stores. Shopify's unauthenticated /products.json endpoint makes it trivially scrapeable. eBay Browse API access to pawn seller stores is also real. So collection is genuinely feasible.
triage.latency: The listing data itself has no wire competitor - nobody publishes pawn listing counts, so on raw timing there is a lead of weeks-to-months versus the earnings print. The problem is not latency, it is that the series does not measure what the thesis claims.
triage.already_priced: Not priced by the market, but the scraping layer is a commodity: multiple vendors sell turnkey Shopify products.json harvesters (Apify 'Shopify Product Scraper', ShopScraping, Simplescraper, Tendem.ai). Any fund that wants a Shopify catalog time series buys it off the shelf for pocket change - the 'nobody time-series it' moat is a build-vs-buy question, not a barrier.
triage.biggest_doubt: That online listing velocity is a merchandising decision, not a forfeiture census. EZCORP disclosed online sales are only ~9% of sales volume and grew 21% YoY on a deliberate digital push (instant-quote tool now in 66% of US stores, online payments +42%). A scraper would read that channel-migration ramp as a surge in consumer default. The idea's own risk section names this confound and it turns out to be the dominant term, not a footnote.
triage.reason: The mechanism is broken three ways: (a) the online catalog is ~9% of sales volume and is growing 21% YoY for reasons unrelated to defaults, so listing velocity mostly measures EZCORP's e-commerce buildout; (b) the underlying ratio is famously inert - EZCORP's disclosed redemption rate has sat at 76-77% across wildly different macro regimes, so there is little cyclical signal to extract, and the actual earnings driver management points to is pawn loans outstanding (+33% YoY), which the catalog does not observe; (c) jewelry scrapping is 18.2% of revenue and that forfeited gold goes to the smelter, never appearing as a listing, so the gold-heavy stress mix the thesis most wants is systematically invisible. The 'skeletal coverage' edge claim is also wrong for the larger leg - FirstCash is an ~$8.8B market cap name with ~400K ADV and real sell-side coverage, not a neglected microcap.

triage.name: Screwworm Frontline Bulletin Watch
triage.data_exists: Yes, and more abundantly than the idea assumes. SENASICA publishes 'Boletin Informativo Avance GBG' bulletins (No. 03, No. 11, etc.) on gob.mx, runs a zoosanitary page for 'miasis por gusano barrenador del ganado', and - critically - has launched a public dashboard tracking NWS cases across Mexico. COPEG and APHIS stakeholder notices are real. Data availability is not the failure point.
triage.latency: There is no Spanish-language lead. USDA/APHIS issues its own English press releases announcing Mexican SENASICA confirmations (e.g. 'Mexico Confirms Case of New World Screwworm in Nuevo Leon', published by both USDA and APHIS), APHIS maintains a live screwworm.gov current-status page, and USDA states the SENASICA dashboard is what enhances its own ability to monitor south of the border. USDA is wired directly into the same feed, and Mexican general press (El Imparcial, El Siglo de Durango) carries detections same-day.
triage.already_priced: Heavily. This has been the single most-watched North American animal-health story for two years; Drovers ran 'Fear, Not Fundamentals, Drive Cattle Sell-Off on Mexican Border News,' and prior announcements produced $5/cwt moves and limit-down deferred feeder sessions - i.e. the market repriced within one session, not over days. The idea's own risk note that the pattern has been learned since 2025 is correct and decisive.
triage.biggest_doubt: The regime has inverted since this idea was written. US southern ports have been closed since May 2025; as of July 2026 USDA announced a phased REOPENING beginning Aug 24, 2026 (Douglas AZ first, then Santa Teresa and Columbus NM). The tradable event is no longer 'detection triggers closure' but 'does USDA pause a reopening,' which USDA explicitly frames as discretionary - contingent on post-opening audits of Sonora and Chihuahua, not on detection geography. The mechanical detection-to-closure mapping the thesis rests on no longer holds.
triage.reason: The claimed edge - Spanish bulletins posting before English coverage - does not survive contact: APHIS press-releases Mexican confirmations itself and consumes the same SENASICA dashboard, so there is no informational lead. The trigger rule is also stale and now discretionary under a reopening regime. Execution compounds it: feeder cattle futures have no micro contract, one GF is roughly $180-200K notional, and CME expands limits by 50% after a limit settle - so precisely when a headline is big enough to matter, GF locks limit and the 'enter within hours' fill does not exist.

triage.name: Lock Queue (Army Corps LPMS outage telemetry)
triage.data_exists: Yes, fully. The Corps Locks portal (ndc.ops.usace.army.mil/ords/r/lpms/corps-locks) publicly serves a Lock Queue Flotilla Report ('most recent vessels waiting to pass through a lock') and a Lock Status Report ('current operating condition of each lock'), both refreshing every 15 minutes, free and without login. Data Web Services endpoints exist. This is the cleanest data source of the four.
triage.latency: The telemetry is near-real-time, but the lead is against the wrong counterparty. USACE describes the intended users as commercial barge operators and commodity shippers who check the lock queue to plan navigation - meaning the exact merchants who set interior grain basis already watch this natively and intraday. Major planned outages are announced months ahead (Lock 25's Aug 10-Sep 19 daytime closures), and unscheduled ones propagate immediately via Corps navigation notices, carrier pages like ACBL's river-closures list, and USDA's agtransport.usda.gov barge dashboard.
triage.already_priced: By the physical market, essentially instantly - barge freight and interior basis reprice the same day because the people trading them are the people reading the queue report. The idea's premise that ag desks learn days later via USDA transport reports understates how fast the cash trade moves.
triage.biggest_doubt: Instrument mismatch. The documented economic impact of lock outages and low water lands on barge freight rates (Memphis rates ran 40% above three-year average) and on interior cash basis (corn basis blowing out ~40 cents versus the five-year average) - a wealth transfer from farmer to elevator. It largely does not move CBOT flat price, because global corn supply and demand is unchanged by a stuck tow. A small trader cannot trade interior basis, and barge freight swaps are illiquid.
triage.reason: Genuine data with no tradable expression for a small trader in the named instruments. The convexity lives in cash basis and barge freight, not in CBOT corn futures or calendar spreads, and ADM (~$30B) and MOS are far too large for a multi-day lock outage to register in quarterly EPS. Combined with the base rate - the idea concedes only multi-day failures at true chokepoints qualify, which is roughly one or two events a year - the expected move in the tradable instruments is too small and too rare to clear spread, commissions, and carry.

triage.name: German Tank Checkout
triage.data_exists: Partially, and unevenly across the named targets. Shopify order numbers are still sequential by default (fresh stores start at 1001 and increment by one), so the raw counter exists on Shopify-hosted merchants. But Shopify now interposes a random, non-sequential Confirmation Number on the thank-you page during high-concurrency periods, third-party apps mask sequences, and Revolve and 1-800-Flowers do not run on Shopify's counter at all. There is no single obtainable series across the four names.
triage.latency: In principle weeks ahead of the print, since the counter is observable the moment you transact. That part is fine; the failure is estimator validity and target selection, not timing.
triage.already_priced: Not a packaged vendor product - the idea is right that no data firm will run ToS-violating probe orders. But that is a legal moat, not an information moat, and it cuts against the operator too: repeatedly placing and cancelling orders to harvest a competitor's ledger is a terms-of-service breach with chargeback and fraud exposure, plus real cash outlay and return friction every week.
triage.biggest_doubt: One of the four named targets no longer exists as a DTC business. Allbirds agreed in April 2026 to sell the Allbirds brand and footwear assets to American Exchange Group and is pivoting to AI compute infrastructure under the name 'NewBird AI' - so BIRD's ~$99M equity is now driven by a compute story, and its shoe order count is uncorrelated with the stock. Separately, the statistical claim is misstated: a week-over-week delta between two observed IDs is a counter difference, not the German tank estimator, and it is only unbiased if the counter is global, monotonic, and increments exactly once per revenue-bearing order - false where merchants run separate US/EU/UK storefront instances, draft and test orders, and multi-channel fulfillment.
triage.reason: The target list is broken (BIRD is no longer a footwear company; RVLV and FLWS are not on Shopify's sequential counter), the estimator does not do what is claimed, and the order-to-revenue bridge runs through AOV and mix - the actual volatile terms - so 'essentially zero sampling error' is false even where the counter is clean. Layer on ~13 noisy observations per quarter against companies with material wholesale, retail, and international revenue outside the sampled checkout, thin options in the small names, and a collection method that requires ToS-violating transactions, and there is no executable edge here.

triage.name: Store-Leader Posting Geocoder
triage.data_exists: Yes - verified CAVA GM postings carry full street addresses (e.g. 1111 Miamisburg Centerville Rd, Washington Twp OH), and brands run public ATS/store-locator feeds. But the core 'edge' claim is false: Thinknum sells a daily Job Listings dataset AND a daily Store Locations dataset that explicitly 'track store opening and closings in real time' (thinknum.com/datasets/store, /datasets/job_listings), distributed via Snowflake. The address payload is a productized commercial dataset, not bespoke work no vendor will do.
triage.latency: Negative-to-zero lead. Local news already scrapes these postings and publishes the address the same week (WDTN/Yahoo ran the CAVA Centerville address straight off the job posting). Building permits, lease filings, and local 'what now' outlets typically surface a site months BEFORE a GM is hired, so the posting is a lagging indicator of location knowledge, not a leading one.
triage.already_priced: Yes. Unit-growth guidance is reaffirmed quarterly and rarely varies: CAVA guided 75-77 net new restaurants for FY2026 and reaffirmed it at Q2. Openings are the most pre-announced, lowest-variance line in the model.
triage.reason: The signal predicts the wrong variable. CAVA's +12% post-Q2-2026 move came from 9% same-restaurant sales and 5.3% traffic, not the 17 net openings against a reaffirmed 75-77 guide - a pipeline tracker accurate to plus/minus 2-3 units forecasts a number the market already has. Compounded by the edge being demonstrably wrong: store-location and job-listing data with geography are both daily commercial products, and local media already publish the addresses off the same postings.

triage.name: Heat-Dome Miner Curtailment Credits
triage.data_exists: Partially, with a factual error in the universe. ERCOT's Public API (apiexplorer.ercot.com, /rt/spp endpoint, free with registration, OpenAPI 3.0 spec, 106 endpoints) genuinely provides real-time LMPs, load, and 4CP data. RIOT (Rockdale/Corsicana) and CIFR (Odessa/Black Pearl) are ERCOT. WULF is NOT - Lake Mariner and Cayuga are NYISO, and Abernathy is SPP - so a third of the named universe has no ERCOT curtailment exposure whatsoever.
triage.latency: ERCOT prices publish in real time, so the raw input has no latency advantage over anyone who wants it. Miner curtailment is also visible same-day in network hashrate and is covered within days by TheMinerMag; Luxor's Hashrate Index publishes dedicated public explainers on miner 4CP economics and ERCOT demand-response participation. The claimed 'gap between two analyst communities' is already occupied by free published research.
triage.already_priced: Largely, and the lever has structurally collapsed. The $31.7M August-2023 record came when RIOT was a pure-play miner; by November 2025 monthly credits were roughly $1.0M curtailment plus $1.3M demand response. RIOT is now an ~$8B market cap with a $9.1B 20-year AI lease and an AMD Rockdale lease - a $10-30M credit line is a rounding error against AI-lease headlines and BTC beta.
triage.reason: The economic lever the whole thesis rests on is being contractually dismantled: converting Rockdale and Corsicana to AI/HPC tenants removes exactly the curtailable load that generated the credits, and recent monthly credits are two orders of magnitude below the 2023 record against a market cap that grew several-fold. Even a perfect model of an August heat dome predicts a low-single-digit-million line item inside a monthly release whose price reaction is dominated by BTC and datacenter leasing news.

triage.name: Sphere Occupancy Cam
triage.data_exists: Yes, and it is trivially public - Sphere runs its own official 24/7 Exosphere livestream (thesphere.com/xo-stream, presented by Verizon), plus multiple 24/7 YouTube streams, SkylineWebcams, and camscape feeds. There is no scarcity in the observation.
triage.latency: The observation is continuous and real-time, but the target variable is never disclosed, so there is nothing to be early to. Verified in the filings: Exosphere advertising revenue is NOT separately reported - it is bundled with sponsorship, signage, and suite license fees in both the 10-K and quarterly releases. There is no line item the webcam index can be scored against.
triage.already_priced: The advertising itself is a public billboard seen by millions and posted constantly to social media by the advertisers themselves, and Sphere streams it officially. Any inflection visible on a webcam is visible to the entire internet simultaneously.
triage.reason: The measurement can never be converted to dollars: ad pricing is undisclosed, house promo occupies board time that generates ticket rather than ad revenue, and the revenue line is bundled with sponsorship and suite fees. The magnitude also fails - the entire combined sponsorship/Exosphere/suite line moved $10.5M on $226.4M of Q2 2026 Sphere segment revenue ($313.6M company-wide), so even a large occupancy swing is swamped by attendance, the show slate, Abu Dhabi expansion, and Dolan governance headlines.

triage.name: FECM Export-Order Sniper
triage.data_exists: Yes, though the idea names a stale office - the LNG export docket moved from FECM to DOE's Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office (energy.gov/hgeo). The 2026 orders listing is real, public, and scrapable, showing 89 dated orders from Jan 12 to Aug 12, 2026, each with order number, docket number, issuance date, and holder.
triage.latency: Effectively none on the orders that matter. DOE issues its own press release on material grants - the Commonwealth LNG non-FTA authorization was announced by Secretary Wright alongside President Trump at the White House the same day the order issued. Applications and notices run through the Federal Register on a published schedule, and the LNG docket is a full-time beat for NGI, Reuters, Platts, and Argus, who cover filings same-day.
triage.already_priced: Yes, structurally. DOE has now issued 45 long-term authorizations totaling 55.9 Bcf/d as of June 30, 2026; the export pause is reversed and grants are the expected default. DOE is no longer the binding gate on FID - FERC, offtake, and financing are - so an approval confirms consensus rather than surprising it.
triage.reason: The tradeable population is close to empty: of 89 orders in 2026 YTD, almost all are blanket import/export authorizations, corporate name changes, commencement-deadline extensions, and vacations, and the rare genuine new authorizations went to private sponsors (Commonwealth, Argent) with no listed equity. Denials are essentially nonexistent, so the short leg does not exist, and a single incremental authorization ten years forward will not move Henry Hub calendar spreads above noise in an instrument whose notional is already awkward for a small trader.

triage.name: OIR Cat Data-Call Tape
triage.data_exists: Partially. floir.gov/tools-and-data/catastrophe-reporting is real, with per-storm pages for Ian, Helene, Milton, Michael and Irma, updated on an event-driven cadence (Milton data calls began 10/10/2024, updates through 12/2025). BUT the page states OIR publishes only aggregated data 'in summary reports... to provide the general public with information' — claims counts, paid and case-incurred losses by line, county/ZIP maps. There are NO per-company breakdowns, which is the leg the whole trade rests on. The premise 'where per-company breakdowns are published' is false.
triage.latency: Negative. FLOIR posts to a public-facing website and trade press picks it up within hours. Insurance Journal ran OIR's Milton tally (152,180 claims, $1.9bn estimated insured loss) on 10/15/2024, six days after landfall; Insurance Business, Newsweek and weather.com all republish OIR figures as routine news. The scrape reaches you at the same moment the wire does.
triage.already_priced: Yes, and by faster sources. KCC (~$36bn), Moody's RMS ($22-36bn), Verisk ($30-50bn) and CoreLogic ($17-28bn) publish industry loss estimates within days of landfall and those are what move UVE/HCI/HRTG/RNR. Individual carriers also pre-announce: Heritage publicly flagged a Milton loss reaching its third reinsurance layer (>$450m) well before its 8-K. The regulator's tape trails the vendor range, it does not lead it.
triage.reason: The data is aggregate-only, so the stated collection step (map per-company breakdowns to tickers) cannot be executed at all. Even the aggregate is republished by Insurance Journal and mainstream press within days, giving zero informational lead, and the price-setting inputs post-landfall are the vendor cat-model ranges plus company pre-announcements, both of which are faster. Instruments are fine (UVE/HCI/HRTG/SLDE all trade with options) but there is nothing to trade on.
triage.biggest_doubt: The one residual: the shape of the loss-development curve (open vs closed claims, reopen rates) is genuinely under-covered by press that only quotes headline dollars, and reserve-adequacy reads on Florida names have historically been profitable. But without per-company data you cannot convert a curve read into a single-name position, and reinsurance attachment points make the aggregate-to-EPS map non-monotonic.

triage.name: Royalty Drip Nowcast
triage.data_exists: Real but gated. WBS noteholder reports exist and do contain the fields claimed — Planet Fitness Master Issuer's quarterly noteholder report carries Quarterly Payment Date and Quarterly Collection Period begin/end, and the deals carry system-wide-sales-linked DSCR triggers. But these are 144A deals: the manager delivers the report to 'offered noteholders and other parties' via trustee websites. Computershare CTSLink grants access by registration plus additional approval, with data vendors (Bloomberg, Trepp, Intex) admitted only 'by request of the Depositor,' and users recertify on each login that they will not disseminate the information without the Depositor's written consent. A non-QIB retail trader cannot hold the notes and therefore cannot certify in.
triage.latency: Structurally unreliable and sometimes negative. Reports are quarterly and delivered the business day before the quarterly determination date, on the deal's calendar, not the fiscal quarter's — so for a given fiscal quarter the report frequently lands after the earnings date (the idea's own risk note concedes this). Wingstop's FQ4-2025 print was 2/18/2026; the covering collection period does not clear the trustee in time to be reliably ahead of it.
triage.already_priced: Yes for the highest-value prints. Planet Fitness pre-releases the exact metric: its January 'Key Year-End Metrics' press release disclosed 20.8m members and full-year system-wide same-club sales +6.7% weeks before the Q4 report. Wingstop has a history of pre-announcing preliminary Q4 system-wide sales at ICR (8-K, Jan 2019). Separately Bloomberg, Trepp and Intex already ingest these trustee reports wholesale, so the 'nobody reads it' premise is wrong.
triage.reason: The reports are contractually restricted to noteholders and expressly bar redistribution, and a small trader cannot become a QIB noteholder in a 144A deal to get access — so the data is not obtainable as described. Where it is obtainable it usually lands on or after the earnings date, and the two cleanest names (PLNT, WING) publicly pre-announce the very metric the trade tries to back-solve.
triage.biggest_doubt: The arithmetic is genuinely clean for pure-franchise perimeters like Wingstop (royalty receipts / royalty rate = system sales), and if someone did have legitimate noteholder access the mid-quarter reads on DRVN or JACK are under-covered. The kill rests on access and timing, not on the mechanism being wrong.

triage.name: Upgrade-Wave Telemetry
triage.data_exists: Yes, exactly as described and better than claimed. Verizon Master Trust, CIK 0001844964, files monthly 10-Ds on EDGAR; I pulled the December-2025 filing (acc. 0001193125-26-030245) and its Exhibit 99.1 reports 'Number of Receivables Upgraded 50,646' current period / 1,296,085 to date, 'Principal Balance of Receivables Upgraded $21,644,444.53', 'Upgrade payments', 'Upgrade Prepayments', plus prepayments and pool balance. Free, structured, trivially scrapeable. This is the one factual claim in the four that fully checks out.
triage.latency: Fails precisely where it matters. 10-Ds file 23-30 days after month-end: Dec-2025 period filed 2026-01-30, Nov filed 2025-12-31, Oct filed 2025-11-26. Apple reported FQ1 2026 on 2026-01-29 — the December file, the peak month of the iPhone 17 launch quarter, landed one day AFTER the print. Only Oct and Nov are available pre-earnings, not the 'weeks before' the thesis assumes.
triage.already_priced: Yes. Verizon discloses its postpaid upgrade rate directly in its own quarterly earnings release (e.g. 2.8%, -20bps y/y), and Verizon reports before Apple. Sell-side already runs exactly this trade — UBS published research titled 'Verizon results are suggesting soft U.S. iPhone demand,' noting ~70% of US iPhones move through carriers and the US is ~30% of global sell-through. The ABS pool also has no handset-brand split, so iPhone and Android upgrades are indistinguishable.
triage.reason: Real, free, high-quality data, but the carrier publishes the same upgrade signal in its own earnings ahead of Apple and the sell-side already trades it, so there is no informational lead. The December 10-D physically arrives after Apple's January print, and the trust data cannot separate iPhone from Android — the specific inference the trade needs.
triage.biggest_doubt: The monthly granularity and the loan-level upgrade count are genuinely richer than Verizon's rounded quarterly percentage, and the delinquency series is a real early consumer-credit read. If the target were VZ/TMO credit rather than AAPL units, this would be closer to a call — but AAPL is the wrong instrument and a single US carrier is far too thin a slice of global units to move a $4T name.

triage.name: Import Alert Ambush
triage.data_exists: Yes. accessdata.fda.gov/cms_ia is live, Import Alert 66-40 (India, drug CGMP, DWPE) is real, and there is an 'Import Alerts by Publish Date' index with per-firm 'Date Published' fields. But it contradicts the 'no feed' edge claim: FDA maintains a publish-date-sorted listing and RSS. Additions relevant to the named issuers are rare — the most recent red-list publish date visible on 66-40 was 05/23/2025.
triage.latency: Negative. FDA notifies the firm before the public page updates, and Indian issuers are obliged to file with BSE/NSE immediately. Sun Pharma's Halol import alert was disclosed by the company in an exchange intimation dated 9 September 2025, and that filing is what FiercePharma, PharmExec and the Indian wires reported. The exchange filing is the first market artifact, not the FDA page.
triage.already_priced: Yes, and the monitoring is a commercial product. Redica Systems and FDAzilla sell FDA enforcement and import-alert monitoring (FDAzilla Intelligence Monitoring Service), FDAImports runs an import-alert practice, and Redica's own guidance notes import alerts 'are published almost daily and are straightforward to monitor.' Plant-to-ticker mapping is standard sell-side pharma coverage, not uncurated ground.
triage.reason: The regulated company discloses the import alert to its exchange the same day, so the market learns first and the FDA page is a confirming artifact, not a lead. Monitoring is already sold as a subscription product by at least two vendors. On top of that the instruments mostly fail: Sun Pharma, Aurobindo and Cipla are NSE/BSE-only with no US listing, Hikma is LSE with only an illiquid OTC ADR, leaving essentially RDY as the sole tradeable name for an event that hits a given issuer roughly once a year.
triage.biggest_doubt: FDA does occasionally post additions with erratic lag in both directions, and there are cases where a small US-listed customer of a detained plant reacts days late. But that residual depends on rare, small-cap second-order names, not the ADRs named here, and it is not a repeatable book.

triage.name: CBER Flu-Lot Release Ledger
triage.data_exists: NO — the source is dead and was never what the idea describes. The FDA CBER page 'Seasonal Information for Influenza Virus Vaccine' (fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/lot-release/seasonal-information-influenza-virus-vaccine) carries the statement: 'CBER will no longer post lot release information for seasonal influenza vaccines after June 2022.' Prior-season archives show the data was LOT COUNTS per product (2014-15: Fluzone 38 lots, Fluarix 6, Fluarix Quadrivalent 29; 2008-09: Fluzone 86, Fluarix 28), not weekly cumulative DOSES by manufacturer. The weekly cumulative-doses series the idea actually describes is CDC's (data.cdc.gov 'Weekly Cumulative Doses (in Millions) of Influenza Vaccines Distributed by Season'), which is aggregate across manufacturers and cannot be split by Sanofi/GSK/CSL.
triage.latency: Moot — the FDA feed has published nothing since June 2022, so there is no cadence at all. The surviving CDC substitute is a manufacturer-reported aggregate posted on a public Socrata open-data portal with API access, i.e. maximally distributed, and it lags shipment rather than leading it.
triage.already_priced: The only live replacement (CDC weekly cumulative doses) is a fully public open-data API endpoint, trivially scraped and already used by public-health and sell-side researchers. Nothing proprietary remains.
triage.reason: The named data source was discontinued after June 2022 and, even when live, contained lot counts rather than the weekly dose ledger the mechanism depends on. The mechanical shipment-nowcast premise collapses; the only surviving series is aggregate, non-attributable CDC open data. Separately, flu vaccines are a low-single-digit revenue slice of SNY and GSK, so even a perfect nowcast would not move diversified-major consensus.

triage.name: Embargo Clock
triage.data_exists: Yes, but it is not proprietary. Rotten Tomatoes score pages are public and pollable, and Kalshi runs live Rotten Tomatoes score markets (KXRT series — kalshi.com/category/culture/rotten-tomatoes) with per-title contracts settling on the Monday after opening. Embargo dates circulate openly via critic posts on X/Bluesky and trade newsletters before release.
triage.latency: No lead. A late embargo is itself a reported news event — trades and outlets run 'reviews embargoed until release day' stories ahead of opening, so the tell is public at the same moment it becomes observable. There is no window in which you know the embargo is late and the market does not.
triage.already_priced: Decisively. Kalshi's OWN official newsletter ('Making Money with Rotten Tomatoes Movie Markets — Kalshi Kit', news.kalshi.com) teaches embargo timing as the Phase-1 pre-embargo signal for exactly these contracts, quoting trader Gaeten Dugas: 'Later embargo dates are often signs that they don't want bad reviews out there early.' The exchange publishes the thesis to its own traders, and the same article flags Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes — its most-traded market at 675,000+ contracts — as the case where the embargo tell failed.
triage.reason: The claimed edge ('never quantified, no vendor, looks too soft to be data') is factually wrong: the venue where the idea proposes to trade markets this exact signal in its own how-to newsletter, and cites its own counterexample. The equity leg is worse — a single opening weekend is a small fraction of CNK/IMAX quarterly box office, and NCMI is a microcap, so option premium on one film's reviews is not covered by the diluted move.

triage.name: Depot Watch
triage.data_exists: Yes — SteamDB (steamdb.info) publicly exposes depot lists, branch names, package rows, and build history, including for unannounced apps, and the Steam Web API is free. The site's own FAQ warns developers not to name depots/branches after unannounced titles precisely because the metadata is public.
triage.latency: Zero to negative lead. SteamDB changes are relayed in minutes by dedicated public bots and X accounts and picked up by press the same day — e.g. a hidden Steam package update surfaced as a SteamDB screenshot posted by the 'Steam Hardware Updates' X account, propagated to Reddit, and became a Notebookcheck news article on the Steam Machine within hours. Any GTA VI-adjacent row would be a wire story before an options order filled.
triage.already_priced: Yes. SteamDB is one of the most-watched leak surfaces in gaming, monitored continuously by tens of thousands of users plus automated change-feed bots; depot/branch appearances are immediately amplified by GTA BOOM, GamesRadar, gamingbible and insider accounts like Tez2, so the price-relevant news is public and mass-distributed at the moment of publication.
triage.reason: The flagship trade is structurally impossible: GTA VI ships November 19, 2026 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S only — console-first, with Zelnick confirming the strategy, no PC version announced, no PC date, and no Steam page. Take-Two emits no Steam depot signal for the title that drives its DCF, and PC is estimated years out. For the remaining publishers the data is real but instantly and loudly public, so there is no informational lead to monetize.

triage.name: Preorder Counter Arb
triage.data_exists: Only partly. Ktown4u is a real retailer with preorder pages, but I checked its album listing (ktown4u.com/newprod_album) and found no official live running cumulative preorder counter per release — the counters the idea assumes are largely fan-reconstructed. Hanteo/Circle first-week charts do exist and are public.
triage.latency: Negative — the market gets the target number by press release, not by scraping. Agencies and distributors publish official cumulative preorder totals directly: YG Plus and Universal announced TWS 'NO TRAGEDY' at 1,022,807 preorders; Belift Lab announced ENHYPEN 'DESIRE: UNLEASH' at 2.18M; Stray Kids '5-STAR' at 4.93M; ZEROBASEONE at 1.08M in 13 days — each carried immediately by Soompi, allkpop and Korean wires. Fan accounts on X also post real-time Ktown4u tracking. Korean retail and sell-side see the same figure at the same time or sooner.
triage.already_priced: Yes. The preorder total is a promoted marketing milestone — the agencies themselves push it as PR because a big number is bullish signaling, and stan accounts publish running tallies for free. It is the single most-watched KPI for these tickers among the Korean retail base that dominates their volume.
triage.reason: The information reaches the market through company PR and free fan trackers before any scraped partial sum could be edged, which is the classic no-lead kill. Execution also fails: KOSDAQ/KOSPI entertainment names have no retail-accessible listed options, and the short leg is not available to a small foreign trader — Korea ran a full short-selling ban from November 2023 into 2025 and KRX was again examining a temporary ban and tighter price limits as of July 2026, with borrow on KOSDAQ names effectively unobtainable. A long-only version keeps all the risk with none of the claimed edge.

triage.name: Square-Money Hold Nowcast
triage.data_exists: Yes — verified all three legs. The Odds API (the-odds-api.com) sells historical/closing lines; Action Network publishes free public betting & money percentage pages per sport (actionnetwork.com/nfl/public-betting, /nba/, /mlb/, /ncaaf/), with deeper access behind Action PRO; VSIN and DraftKings' own splits page (dknetwork.draftkings.com/draftkings-sportsbook-betting-splits) publish the same. Scores are free. The reconstruction is buildable.
triage.latency: The underlying facts publish instantly — game outcomes are public the moment games end, and splits are posted pre-game. There is no lead over the market at all; the 'data' and the 'news' are the same object. The only lag is to the state revenue prints (NJ DGE monthly) and earnings, and everyone watching the stock already has the same scores.
triage.already_priced: Yes, demonstrably and within hours. Benzinga ran 'What's Going On With DraftKings Stock Monday? — DraftKings Faces Parlay Blow As NFL Betting Action Heats Up' (Sept 2025), pricing a specific +2400 prepackaged parlay tailed by ~37,000 users into the stock the next trading morning. Citizens analyst Jordan Bender said the Q2 2026 miss 'was largely expected given unfavorable sports outcomes.' DKNG itself uses the phrase 'customer-friendly sport outcomes' in disclosure. Sell-side explicitly flags post-kickoff weakness as a modeled risk.
triage.biggest_doubt: The core edge claim — 'the betting-data community and the equity community don't talk' — is factually false. The mainstream financial press (Benzinga, TipRanks, Legal Sports Report) writes the Monday-morning hold story, and DKNG trades on it same-day. Even if your hold reconstruction is more precise than the crowd's, you are competing on estimation quality against a market that already knows the sign, not exploiting an information gap.
triage.reason: The signal's inputs are public simultaneously with the market's knowledge of them — scores are the news. DKNG/FLUT reprice on bettor-friendly weekends within one trading session, with mainstream coverage naming the exact parlays, and analysts pre-condition estimates on sport outcomes. There is no informational lead, only a marginal modeling-precision claim against a crowded, well-watched name.

triage.name: Call Report Amendment Autopsy
triage.data_exists: Yes — verified in detail. FFIEC CDR Public Data Distribution offers both bulk downloads (cdr.ffiec.gov/public/PWS/DownloadBulkData.aspx, tab-delimited and XBRL, per reporting period) and a free-registration SOAP Public Web Service with a RetrieveFacsimile method returning per-institution, per-period facsimiles, documented in CDR-PDD-SIS-611 v1.10. An open-source wrapper exists (github.com/call-report/ffiec-data-connect) plus a REST reference at call.report/api. FFIEC docs confirm amended Call Reports 'may be submitted at any time to correct reporting errors' and are also demanded by Call Report Analysts and examiners. Crucially, CDR serves the latest facsimile, not a version history — so daily snapshotting is the only way to build the diff, which is exactly what makes it uncrowded.
triage.latency: Mixed but genuinely favorable on the load-bearing leg. Original call reports land ~30 days after quarter-end, which is AFTER a listed bank's earnings release (~2 weeks) — so no lead on headline numbers — but ~10-15 days BEFORE the 10-Q (40-45 day deadline), with far more granularity than a thin community-bank earnings release. Amendments are the real signal: a resubmission can hit any day, triggers no 8-K, no press release, and no newswire item. That is a clean, dated, public-but-unwatched event.
triage.already_priced: No evidence of it. Vendors (BankRegData, call.report, S&P) redistribute CDR data as point-in-time levels; I could not find any product exposing a versioned amendment-diff stream, and call.report's own API docs are silent on versioning. One caveat: RC-O uninsured-deposit memo lines specifically became heavily scraped post-SVB in 2023 and should be treated as crowded — the RI-E free-text itemizations and the amendment diff itself are not.
triage.biggest_doubt: Tradeability at the small end. The idea targets $200M-$2B banks, which mostly have no listed options, thin borrow, and wide spreads — the short leg is often not executable even in small size. The workable universe is the $1-10B listed regionals where borrow exists, which shrinks the sample. Second doubt: the idea concedes most amendments are clerical, so the whole thing lives or dies on a benign-vs-adverse taxonomy that has to be built before you know whether the base rate supports a trade.
triage.reason: This is the only one of the four with a verified, real informational asymmetry: a call report amendment is a quasi-restatement that is publicly filed, requires no SEC announcement, and is invisible unless you snapshot and diff yourself — which no vendor appears to do. The data is free, API-accessible, and pullable daily. Advance to build the amendment taxonomy and measure the base rate, but restrict the tradeable universe up-front to names with real borrow and spread.

triage.name: Warranty Fine-Print Retreat
triage.data_exists: Partially, and it is the wrong data. Warranty PDFs and terms pages are public and Wayback-crawlable, so the crawler is buildable. But I searched specifically for coverage retreats at the named companies and found none: Hyundai's 10yr/100k powertrain warranty is intact for MY2026 with the same original-owner/5yr-60k-transfer structure it has had for two decades; SolarEdge still shows 12-year standard inverter, 25-year optimizer, 10-year battery with paid extensions; Generac is actively promoting free 7-year extended warranties. The event I would be trading on does not appear to occur.
triage.latency: Poor in both directions. Warranty terms are marketing collateral — dealer networks, promo pages, and the trade press amplify changes immediately (Generac's spring promo was on dealer blogs and Facebook within days). And the mechanism's own lag is the killer: fine print applies to units sold going forward, so it takes model-year cycles to reach the P&L, far beyond a 2-6 week horizon.
triage.already_priced: The warranty signal that actually matters is already a mature commercial product. Warranty Week has tracked claims paid, accruals, reserves, and change-of-estimate for 1,400+ US manufacturers since 2003, capturing >99% of available data, and publishes company-level numbers (Generac $101M accruals in 2025, +29% YoY; SolarEdge $70M, +16%). ASC 460 forces quarterly disclosure of exactly the reserve builds this idea is trying to anticipate.
triage.biggest_doubt: The sign is backwards or at best ambiguous. Shortening coverage REDUCES future warranty liability — it is margin-accretive going forward, which is why an actuarially-driven cut could just as easily be read bullish. Meanwhile warranty length is set competitively (Hyundai's 10/100k was a brand-positioning weapon, not an actuarial output), so the 'costly admission of bad reliability' reading is not identified. Combine that with a near-zero observed event rate and no 2-6 week transmission channel and there is nothing to trade.
triage.reason: The trigger event is vanishingly rare — I could not find a single coverage retreat at any of the named manufacturers — the transmission to P&L exceeds the stated holding period, the directional sign is ambiguous or inverted, and the genuinely informative warranty variable (accrual and reserve rates) is already disclosed quarterly and commercially productized by Warranty Week.

triage.name: Off-Cycle Audit-Partner Swap
triage.data_exists: Yes. PCAOB AuditorSearch is real, free, and offers a full dataset download updated daily, with a published data-element reference (assets.pcaobus.org AuditorSearch Form AP data references). Engagement partner name and Partner ID have been filed since 2017, so tenure clocks are genuinely computable. The data claim survives; nothing else does.
triage.latency: Fatally backwards. PCAOB Rule 3211 sets the Form AP deadline at 35 days AFTER the auditor's report is first included in a document filed with the SEC (10 days for IPOs). So for a December fiscal-year filer, the 10-K lands ~late February and the partner identity only becomes public ~early April. You learn about the swap after the clean audit opinion is already public — the stated trade, 'short ahead of their next 10-K,' is mechanically impossible for the annual catalyst. What remains is a Q1 10-Q, a review not an audit, which will not surface the dispute.
triage.already_priced: Partly — the dataset is not the obscure corner the idea claims. Ideagen Audit Analytics' audit opinion database explicitly 'integrates the signing partner(s) information and other audit firms in compliance with PCAOB Form AP,' so partner tenure is a shipped commercial field available to every institution on WRDS. AuditorSearch had 2.2M+ searches and 49,383 full-dataset downloads as of end-2022.
triage.biggest_doubt: Even granting the swap detection, the academic evidence gives no usable prior. Studies find no material improvement in audit quality after partner rotation, no evidence a fresh partner uncovers what the predecessor missed, and — pointing the opposite way from the thesis — material misstatements are MORE likely in the first year after rotation due to the learning curve. Benign causes (retirement, office relocation, internal staffing, client-portfolio rebalancing) swamp the adversarial ones, so the base rate of a tradeable adverse outcome per swap is likely near noise.
triage.reason: The 35-day post-audit-report filing lag means Form AP arrives after the very catalyst the trade is built around, inverting the entire timing thesis. The dataset is also already integrated into Audit Analytics' commercial product rather than being unmined, and the academic record offers no reliable sign on partner turnover — leaving a sparse, ambiguous, late signal.

triage.name: Trustee Exit Tape
triage.data_exists: Partially, but the collection channel is broken. EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov) is real, free and daily, and the named distress-specialist trustees are real (ankuratrust.com/expertise/indenture-trustee-services markets itself explicitly for 'stressed and distressed situations... successor indenture trustee'; WSFS replaced Wells Fargo as successor trustee for Walter Investment in 2017). BUT I checked the SEC's Form 8-K instructions (sec.gov/files/form8-k.pdf): Section 6, including Item 6.02 'Change of Servicer or Trustee', applies ONLY to asset-backed securities issuers. An operating company has NO mandatory 8-K item for a trustee resignation. My EDGAR full-text search for 'resignation of trustee'/'successor trustee' returned almost entirely ABS boilerplate — Harley-Davidson Motorcycle Trust, John Deere Owner Trust, Mercedes-Benz Auto Receivables, CWHEQ — none of which has tradeable equity. The corporate cases that matter surface only as a discretionary Item 8.01 or a supplemental-indenture exhibit attached to the next 10-Q/10-K (weeks-to-months lag) or to the Form T-3 filed WITH the exchange offer.
triage.latency: Negative. The filing lags the event, and the event itself lags the news. Hunton's practitioner memo 'Dealing with Bondholders in Troubled Times' confirms the trustee resigns once the credit is already troubled, not in anticipation. Meanwhile Octus (ex-Reorg Research), 9fin and Debtwire are subscription products whose entire franchise is real-time reporting of ad-hoc-group formation, co-op agreements and restructuring prep — they publish this weeks before a supplemental indenture hits EDGAR. You would be reading the paperwork shadow of a story the credit desks already traded.
triage.already_priced: Yes. By the time a distress-specialist trustee is seated, the leveraged issuer's equity is typically already broken — hard-to-borrow with elevated borrow cost, and puts priced for a binary restructuring outcome. The idea's own risk note concedes this and retreats to 'crossover credits where equity still trades as if healthy,' which is a tiny residual population that Octus/9fin cover first anyway.
triage.biggest_doubt: That the tape is even observable in time. If the disclosure vehicle is a supplemental-indenture exhibit filed with the next periodic report, the signal arrives after the coupon date or exchange offer it was supposed to predict — and the daily EDGAR feed is swamped by benign ABS trust housekeeping with no equity to short.
triage.reason: KILL. Item 6.02 is asset-backed-only, so operating-company trustee swaps have no timely mandatory filing — the corporate cases arrive late (periodic-report exhibits) or simultaneously with the restructuring (Form T-3), while the daily EDGAR tape is dominated by tradeable-equity-free ABS boilerplate. Octus/9fin/Debtwire already sell the underlying event in real time, and the equity is usually distressed and expensive to short by the time the paperwork appears.

triage.name: Dividend Clock Slip
triage.data_exists: Yes, and it is free. Nasdaq.com's per-ticker dividend-history pages (nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/<ticker>/dividend-history) carry the declaration date alongside ex/record/pay dates; EODHD's splits-dividends endpoint documents an extended format explicitly including declaration date for major US tickers on a free tier. The authoritative, second-stamped source is the declaration 8-K / press release on EDGAR itself, which is free and needs no vendor. Building per-board cadence baselines is ordinary archival work, not a data-access problem.
triage.latency: This is the structural strength: there is no publication race, because the signal is an inference from an ABSENCE. Nothing gets published that a newswire could beat you to. The baseline is built offline in advance; the flag fires the moment a board's habitual declaration window lapses in silence, and resolution (cut, 'dividend review', or late-but-intact declaration) lands days-to-weeks later. The lead is genuine and structural rather than a scraping-speed advantage.
triage.already_priced: Only partly, and this is the honest weakness. The mechanism is documented in peer-reviewed finance: Kalay & Loewenstein (1986) found cuts occur more often when announcements are late, and 'Can we predict dividend cuts?' (Journal of Corporate Finance, 2016, US firms 1971-2014) found the longer the interval between dividend announcements, the higher the probability of a cut — managers delay bad news. So it is a published anomaly, not a secret. But it is not packaged as a feed or screen: commercial dividend-safety products (Simply Safe Dividends, Dividend.com, OptionMetrics' options-implied approach) rank payout ratio, coverage and options pricing — not declaration timestamps against a per-board baseline. In broad selloffs the cut is priced before the window expires, so the edge lives in quiet-tape idiosyncratic cases.
triage.biggest_doubt: Base rate and false positives. Most delayed declarations resolve benignly (calendar reshuffles, merger integration, board-meeting drift), so a naive put-buying program bleeds premium across many expiries for a few 10-30% payoffs. It needs hard conditioning — coverage below 1x, leverage, prior guidance language — and strict exclusion of microcaps with no listed options or wide put spreads. The published academic support also means a systematic fund could already be running it.
triage.reason: ADVANCE. The data is free and public, the lead is structural rather than a scraping race (you are trading an absence, so nothing beats you to the tape), and the payoff is verified and live: the 2025-26 BDC/mREIT complex is producing real cuts (Monroe Capital -64%, TriplePoint -23%, Two Harbors -13%; median US BDC coverage 0.99x, 0.89x ex-PIK) with double-digit single-session drops, in names with listed options a small trader can access. The published academic precedent is the main discount, not a disqualifier.

triage.name: Top-Mover Carousel
triage.data_exists: Half of it does not. The Coinbase side is computable — Advanced Trade REST market data is public. But the claimed 'Robinhood quote endpoints' are not a public resource: Robinhood has never published a public market-data API, restricts programmatic access to internal and select institutional partners, and its Terms of Service Sec. 3 prohibits 'any robot, spider, other automated device, or manual process to monitor or copy any content from the Service.' The reverse-engineered community API authenticates with personal credentials, breaks on every major app update, and as of 2025-26 is walled behind MFA and device verification. The proposed 'periodic scripted app scrapes' are a ToS violation with account-termination risk, not an infrastructure plan.
triage.latency: Zero. Carousel membership is a deterministic function of 24h percent change — the identical public price data that CoinGecko, CoinMarketCap and every crypto screener already publish in real time, with dedicated gainers/losers/trending endpoints. Thousands of retail 'top gainer' bots (3Commas, OctoBot, TradingView webhook-to-Coinbase alert chains) already fire on exactly this trigger automatically. You are not front-running the notification wave; you are entering after a 20%+ move alongside every other momentum bot watching the same number.
triage.already_priced: Yes, and the effect is famous rather than obscure. Barber, Huang, Odean & Schwarz built 'Attention-Induced Trading and Returns' (JFE) specifically on the Robinhood Top Mover list — documenting that herding episodes reliably predict negative returns, which is the very reversal leg proposed here. Robinhood cut off Robintrack's public holder data in August 2020 after this attention became tradeable. The claim that 'crypto quant desks model order flow, not the retail app UI' is contradicted by the existence of an entire retail bot ecosystem keyed to gainers lists.
triage.biggest_doubt: Instrument access on top of the data problem. US persons still cannot trade Coinbase's international 50x perps or stock perps; onshore access only arrived via Coinbase Financial Markets' CFTC approval in mid-2026 and its own perp-style product, which does not cover the mid-cap altcoin universe the strategy targets. And the idea's own risk note is fatal: in thin coins the threshold-crossing move is often itself a pump engineered to harvest the carousel — you would be the exit liquidity.
triage.reason: KILL. The Robinhood half of the data source does not exist publicly and its collection method violates ToS against active anti-automation defenses; the Coinbase half is a deterministic function of price data that every screener publishes and countless retail bots already trade, so there is no lead. The specific attention effect is a widely cited published JFE result, and US retail cannot reach the mid-cap perps the trade requires.

triage.name: Performance-Bond Spiral Forecaster
triage.data_exists: Yes — this is the one thing the idea gets right. CME Clearing advisories are public at cmegroup.com/notices/clearing/ with per-contract rates and effective dates (e.g. notice 25-393 metal margins effective 29 Dec 2025; 26-041 effective 2 Feb 2026). Per CME advisory Chadv21-471, SPAN risk parameter files are downloadable without charge via CME DataMine, the public FTP (ftp.cmegroup.com/pub/span/data/cme) and the website, with separate files for the SPAN and SPAN 2 frameworks. A shadow margin calculation is genuinely buildable.
triage.latency: None — and worse than none, because the dissemination is deliberately broad. CME runs a FREE opt-in mailing list providing advance notification of performance-bond changes to anyone who signs up, and the notices are relayed within minutes by Barchart, FXStreet, the mining/energy trade press and commodity Twitter accounts (which post the full product-by-product breakdown the same evening). Every participant receives the effective date simultaneously. The 'public PDFs almost no one parses' premise is simply false.
triage.already_priced: Yes, and the forecast leg collapses into something already visible. Empirical work (Hedegaard, 'Causes and Consequences of Margin Levels in Futures Markets'; Fed FEDS 2014-86 'An Empirical Analysis of Futures Margin Changes') finds exchanges raise margins AFTER realized volatility spikes and CME hikes quickly following vol spikes — so forecasting the hike is just forecasting realized vol, which the whole market observes in the same prices. Everyone long the contract is already watching their own vol.
triage.biggest_doubt: The directional mechanism is unsupported by the evidence. The literature finds margin increases reduce open interest and volume (speculators cutting more than hedgers) and raise price impact and reduce liquidity — but there is no established directional price effect; the Chicago Fed and ECB work finds mixed-to-no volatility impact and notes exchanges react to vol rather than cause moves. 'Position with the trend into the hike' is momentum wearing a margin costume, and it is entered precisely when spreads are widest.
triage.reason: KILL. The advisories reach the entire market simultaneously through CME's own free advance-notification list and instant newswire/social relay, so there is no informational lead in the reaction leg; the forecast leg reduces to a realized-vol forecast everyone can see, since CME hikes after vol spikes. The claimed price mechanism is contradicted by the margin-change literature (open interest falls, direction does not), and LME nickel is unreachable for a small trader while natgas/cocoa deliver the widest spreads and harshest notional exactly when the hike lands.

triage.name: Leverage-Bracket Diff Bot
triage.data_exists: Yes. GET /fapi/v1/leverageBracket is real and documented (returns notionalFloor/notionalCap, initialLeverage, maintMarginRatio, notionalCoef); OKX position-tier and Bybit risk-limit tables likewise exist. Binance also publishes each change as a support announcement with an explicit effective timestamp (e.g. the MTLUSDT tier update, and the 2026-04-10 14:30 UTC+8 batch covering XPLUSDT/FUSDT/0GUSDT/WIFUSDT).
triage.latency: Negative lead. The API bracket only changes AT the effective time; the public announcement precedes it by hours-to-days. So the diff bot learns the news strictly after the newswire, not before. The only usable window is announcement-to-effective, which is public by construction.
triage.already_priced: Yes, immediately. The Binance announcements page is the most heavily scraped page in crypto (listing/delisting bots, Telegram relays), and these specific tier notices are reprinted within minutes by crypto.news, PANews, blockchain.news. Liquidation/leverage dashboards like CoinGlass already commoditize the risk surface, and every ccxt user pulls brackets for free.
triage.biggest_doubt: Even granting a real deleveraging flow, the affected names are exactly the thin, high-funding alt perps where borrow/funding and slippage are worst, and Binance cuts tiers in batches of dozens of symbols for routine hygiene AFTER volatility rather than as a single-name verdict — so the 'leaked risk-desk opinion' mechanism is mostly absent.
triage.reason: The premise inverts the actual sequence: the exchange announces publicly first and the API only reflects it at the effective time, so there is no informational lead — the diff is a lagging confirmation of an already-wired announcement. Compounding this, the announcement feed is the single most-scraped source in crypto and the tradeable instruments are the illiquid alt perps where costs eat the move.

triage.name: 337 Target-Date Clock
triage.data_exists: Yes. The EDIS RESTful web service is real (base https://edis.usitc.gov/data, XML-only, ~100 resources per page, login.gov registration, no stated fee), and target dates plus Commission determinations publish in the Federal Register. Volume verified: FY2025 had 48 complaints filed / 41 investigations instituted and 25 Final Determinations, 14 finding a violation.
triage.latency: No durable lead where it matters. The ITC posts notices to usitc.gov and Federal Register public inspection simultaneously, and ALJ initial determinations issue confidential-first with the redacted public version filed later — so the claimed 'one-line violation/no-violation machine-readable minutes after posting' is not reliably how the docket behaves.
triage.already_priced: Yes on both legs. The handful of cases with tradeable equities (Apple/Masimo, Sonos/Google type) are the most-watched dockets in IP, with Bloomberg, Reuters and Law360 reporters refreshing in real time, and ITC coverage is already a commercial product (Docket Navigator, Lex Machina, Darts-IP, Law360 IP). The straddle leg is worse: target dates are statutorily published, so market makers price the calendared binary — you pay for the event, you do not harvest it.
triage.biggest_doubt: The barbell problem. Cases where you would genuinely be first involve private Chinese manufacturers and Amazon sellers with nothing to trade; cases with a liquid US-listed respondent are saturated with professional coverage. That leaves maybe a handful of usable events per year, each requiring bespoke import-revenue modeling, with target dates that slip via extension orders and remedies routinely narrowed by design-arounds.
triage.reason: The data is real and free, but the event count with a tradeable, optionable name is a few per year and those are exactly the dockets already watched minute-by-minute by wire reporters and paid IP-analytics products. The scheduled-date straddle is explicitly not an edge because the calendar is published by statute and already in the vol surface.

triage.name: Settlement Choreography Tape
triage.data_exists: Partially, and worse than assumed. CourtListener docket alerts exist but are capped at 5 free (15 with the RECAP extension); ~200 dockets requires a paid membership or bulk commercial rate. PACER RSS coverage is explicitly incomplete: roughly 15 districts publish no RSS feed at all, others publish partial feeds limited to certain document types, and Free Law states it cannot provide complete coverage of everything new in PACER. Minute entries are among the most commonly omitted.
triage.latency: Effectively zero on the names that matter. Roundup and 3M earplug are among the most-reported dockets on earth; mediator appointments and 'trial vacated' entries in MMM or BAYRY become same-hour wire stories. Any lead exists only in obscure dockets whose defendants have no meaningful litigation overhang to compress.
triage.already_priced: Yes. Event-driven funds already run primary-source monitoring on court dockets as standard practice — Visualping alone claims 5 of the top 10 hedge funds by AUM as customers for exactly this kind of page/docket watching — and specialist litigation-analytics products (Lex Machina, Bloomberg Law Litigation Analytics, Docket Alarm, Reorg) cover MDL procedural events commercially.
triage.biggest_doubt: The signal has no established base rate and the idea's own risk note concedes it: court-ordered mediation is a routine formality that usually fails, special masters get appointed in cases that never settle, and sophisticated defendants use mediator appointments as negotiating theater precisely in the high-profile cases where the payoff would be biggest. Selling elevated put skew on a fear-discounted defendant is a short-vol tail trade with an ugly left side if talks collapse into a verdict.
triage.reason: The 'nobody watches this' edge claim is false for exactly the liquid, optionable defendants the trade requires — those dockets are read live by wire reporters and by funds already paying for docket monitoring. The procedural tells are also high-frequency and non-predictive, so the strategy is a short-vol tail bet on a signal with no demonstrated conditional base rate.

triage.name: DART Gap Runner
triage.data_exists: Yes. OpenDART (opendart.fss.or.kr / engopendart.fss.or.kr) is a real free REST API from the FSS requiring only a registered API key, covering KOSPI/KOSDAQ/KONEX filings, and DART auto-feeds KRX's KIND. The ADR mappings (KB, SHG, KEP, PKX, SKM, KT, LPL) are real NYSE listings.
triage.latency: The core premise is now factually wrong. Since 4 March 2025, Korea's Nextrade (NXT) ATS trades 08:00-20:00 KST with an after-market session running 15:40-20:00 — which covers the exact 15:00-19:00 KST filing window the idea depends on. The domestic market is open and prices the filing the same evening, many hours before US pre-market. There is no stale overnight price to run against.
triage.already_priced: Yes, twice over. NXT prices it in Seoul first; then Korean wires (Yonhap Infomax, Edaily, MK) auto-parse the DART/KIND live list instantly and Reuters/Bloomberg Seoul bureaus cover chaebol disclosures within minutes, so the 'hours to a day' English lag is overstated for precisely the large caps that have ADRs. Korean ADR pricing is also an established professional arb — see the SK Hynix ADR premium/conversion-quota episodes.
triage.biggest_doubt: Execution kills whatever residual gap survives. These ADRs are thin in US pre-market with wide spreads, and listed options on PKX/KB/SHG carry negligible open interest and multi-percent bid/ask — a capital-raise dilution short via ADR options cannot clear transaction costs. OpenDART is also a registered-filing batch API keyed on receipt number, not the low-latency live feed the minute-polling design assumes.
triage.reason: The mechanism rests on 'the local market that would price it is closed,' and that stopped being true in March 2025 when Nextrade opened an after-market session to 20:00 KST spanning the entire filing window. With Seoul pricing the filing hours before the US open, plus instant Korean wire pickup and unusable ADR option spreads, there is neither an informational lead nor a tradeable instrument.

triage.name: First-Generic Flash
triage.data_exists: Verified real and free. I queried api.fda.gov/drug/drugsfda.json directly: it returned meta.last_updated = 2026-08-12 against today's 2026-08-13, with 29,265 application records. openFDA's own docs state the drugsfda endpoint refreshes 'Daily (Monday-Friday).' FDA's 'First Generic Drug Approvals' page (fda.gov/drugs/drug-and-biologic-approval-and-ind-activity-reports/first-generic-drug-approvals) and the Orange Book data files are also real and public. The data source is the one part of this idea that checks out.
triage.latency: Backwards from what the idea assumes. FDA transmits the approval letter to the ANDA sponsor privately; the sponsor is the first to know and issues a wire release the same day. Verified examples: Amneal PR'd 'Amneal Receives U.S. FDA Approval for Iohexol Injection' (first generic of GE's Omnipaque) on 2025-11-13, and 'Amneal Announces U.S. FDA Approval of Romidepsin Injection Solution' on 2026-06-04, both on the day of action. The database is a weekday-overnight batch, so an approval on day T surfaces at earliest the morning of T+1 — and my live API pull was already a day stale. The annual First Generic pages update in batches, not in real time.
triage.already_priced: Yes, and by more than one channel. Sponsor press releases hit PR Newswire/Business Wire same day; Drugs.com maintains a free 'New Generic Drug Approvals' running feed; StockTitan runs a live FDA-approvals feed; Citeline/Generics Bulletin, Evaluate and DrugPatentWatch sell this as a commercial product. Separately, the branded incumbent is not surprised either — it is a party to the Paragraph IV litigation and receives notice letters years earlier, so LOE timing is already in sell-side erosion models.
triage.biggest_doubt: That the 'informational lead' runs the wrong direction is fatal on its own, but even granting a lead, the idea's own risk note is decisive: approval is not launch. Patent settlements, 30-month stays and negotiated entry dates routinely put years between an ANDA approval and commercialization, so the approval carries no reliable date for the 80-90% erosion the thesis is built on. Buying puts on that is buying a lottery ticket on litigation you cannot see.
triage.reason: The FDA data is genuine and free, but the sponsor receives the approval letter first and press-releases it the same day while the database updates overnight — the claimed lead is inverted, and free feeds (Drugs.com, StockTitan) plus paid trackers (Citeline, Evaluate, DrugPatentWatch) already cover it. Approval also does not equal launch, so there is no dated event to trade against.

triage.name: EDIS Exclusion-Order Wire
triage.data_exists: Real, and free but gated: edis.usitc.gov requires a Login.gov account plus an EDIS account, and USITC's own 'Who Should Register' guidance confirms even search requires registration. Obtainable at the stated cadence. But the premise that EDIS is the primary public channel is false — USITC runs a parallel public press room with no login at all. I fetched usitc.gov/press_room/initial_determination/090825/certain_vehicle_telematics_fleet_management_and.htm and it renders openly, timestamped 'Monday, September 8, 2025 - 12:00,' naming the investigation (337-TA-1393), the presiding ALJ, and linking the notice PDF. The same holds for institution releases (e.g. /press_room/news_release/2026/er0812_69071.htm) and for Federal Register notices.
triage.latency: No usable lead. The parties are e-served the determination before any public posting and PR it themselves. USITC posts the public notice to its open press room the same day and publishes in the Federal Register days later. Critically, ALJ initial determinations issue in confidential form first — only a short notice is public promptly, with the redacted public version appearing weeks later — so EDIS does not even contain the substance during the window the idea wants to trade. Law360 and Bloomberg Law staff dedicated ITC reporters who file within minutes.
triage.already_priced: Yes. The idea concedes the target dates are 'docketed months in advance' — that is precisely why there is no calendar edge: every statutory target date is in the Federal Register and on USITC's public schedule, so options into those dates carry an event premium. The one genuinely stock-moving 337 of recent years (Masimo/Apple) was the single most-watched IP case in the market, with the ruling wired instantly and the move fully anticipated.
triage.biggest_doubt: The tradable universe is close to empty. Overwhelmingly, 337 complainants and respondents are private firms, foreign manufacturers, or mega-caps that shrug off a single-product ban. Scanning 2026 institutions (energy drinks, foundry coke, child carriers, braiding hair, crafting machines, nanolaminate coatings), almost none map to a US-listed small-cap with liquid options. And determinations are frequently stayed, settled, or dissolved on Presidential review before any economic effect.
triage.reason: The claimed moat — a login-gated system mainstream news scrapes poorly — is verifiably false: USITC publishes the same notices same-day on an open press room page and in the Federal Register, and IP trade press covers 337 intensively. Target dates are public months ahead, so there is no calendar edge, and the set of US-listed small-caps with concentrated 337 exposure and liquid options is nearly empty.

triage.name: Fintech Vintage X-Ray
triage.data_exists: No — the free-data premise fails on verification. I fetched KBRA's U.S. Marketplace Consumer Loan ABS Index (May 2026), which returns 'Log in or Subscribe to KBRA Premium to view this report' — it is not a free publication. Worse, the underlying per-deal trustee data is not public at all: an EDGAR company search for 'Upstart Securitization' returns 'No matching companies,' because these are Rule 144A private placements (Affirm's own releases confirm 144A distribution), so no Reg AB Form 10-D monthly distribution reports are filed. Trustee remittance reports for 144A deals sit behind noteholder-restricted trustee portals. Intex and dv01 are paid institutional products, not free stitching.
triage.latency: Too slow even where obtainable. The KBRA May 2026 index published 5 June 2026 — roughly a one-month lag on top of the trustee remittance cycle itself (reports land ~20-25 days after collection month end). A vintage 'running hot in month two of the quarter' therefore surfaces after the quarter is nearly closed, collapsing the supposed monthly-vs-quarterly asymmetry the whole thesis rests on. The index is also aggregate and collateral-weighted across all rated pools, not per-sponsor per-vintage as the collection plan assumes.
triage.already_priced: This is the definition of an existing commercial product. dv01 — acquired by Fitch Group in 2022 — sells exactly this as 'Market Surveillance,' with turnkey loan-level data across Consumer Unsecured and 16 integrated marketplace platforms, alongside Intex, Finsight and KBRA Premium. Every institutional credit desk that cares already buys it.
triage.biggest_doubt: Even with perfect data the mapping is broken in both directions. Upstart and Affirm sell large whole-loan flows to private credit partners off-securitization, so the securitized sample is adversely selected relative to the retained book that actually drives fair-value marks. And UPST/AFRM marks move at least as much on discount-rate and macro assumptions as on realized credit. Against that, these names carry some of the richest implied vol in US equities into earnings — a noisy, month-late credit read cannot pay for the option premium.
triage.reason: The 'free' data does not exist as described: KBRA's indices sit behind KBRA Premium, and the per-deal trustee reports are 144A-private with no EDGAR 10-D filings (an EDGAR search for Upstart Securitization Trust returns nothing). What is obtainable publishes with a month-plus lag that destroys the monthly-vs-quarterly asymmetry, and dv01/Fitch already sells this exact surveillance commercially.

triage.name: Baby-Bond Call Latency
triage.data_exists: Yes — redemption notices are real, public and instant on EDGAR. But they are not scattered as claimed: issuers file the 8-K and issue a press release simultaneously. Verified 2026 examples: Ellington Financial (28 Jan 2026, Series A at $25.00 plus accrued), JPMorgan Series KK (27 May 2026), BNY Mellon Series H (12 Jun 2026), Northern Trust Series D (3 Aug 2026) — every one an 8-K accompanied by a same-day press release. There is no gap between 'trustee notice,' 'DTCC notice' and 'the wire.'
triage.latency: Zero lead. The press release is the notice. And the audience is not slow: the free retail-income community that owns these issues — Innovative Income Investor's baby bond and $25-par master lists, its 'There Goes Another Preferred' redemption posts and live Bond Discussion board, plus QuantumOnline — flags redemptions within minutes to the precise holder base the thesis claims is asleep. Being fast to an 8-K that was press-released concurrently is not an informational edge.
triage.already_priced: Yes, mechanically and immediately. Called $25-par issues mark to call price plus accrued on the first prints, not over days. Whatever residual premium survives is pennies on a $25 security, against 10-25 cent bid-ask spreads in exactly the illiquid issues the idea targets — the spread eats the convergence.
triage.biggest_doubt: The trade is not executable in the form described. The idea's own risk note concedes borrow is unavailable in tiny preferreds, and there are no listed options on $25-par preferreds or baby bonds, so there is no short leg at all. What remains is 'sell something you already own when it gets called' — portfolio hygiene, not a signal. The second leg, buying sister issues 'likely to be called next,' is an unhedged directional bet on issuer refinancing behavior with no informational basis, and partial calls by lot plus make-whole provisions blur even the convergence target.
triage.reason: Redemption notices are press-released simultaneously with the 8-K (verified across Ellington, JPM, BNY, Northern Trust in 2026) and are broadcast within minutes by free retail-income sites read by this exact holder base, so there is no latency. With no borrow and no listed options, the short leg does not exist, and the residual above-par premium is smaller than the bid-ask in these illiquid issues.

triage.name: 13E-3 Cash-Out Harvest
triage.data_exists: YES — verified real and public. SC 13E-3 is a live EDGAR form type; I pulled actual filings (e.g. sec.gov/Archives/.../knth13e3.htm, BEFUT International SC 13E3, Asia Electrical Power SC 13E3) and confirmed the companion PRE/DEF 14A discloses the exact per-pre-split cash-out price and holder threshold (one example: $0.65/pre-split share to holders of fewer than 150 shares). Free via EDGAR daily index and full-text search. The data leg of this idea is the only one of the four that fully checks out.
triage.latency: No lead at all. The cash-out price is created BY the filing — the filing IS the public announcement. There is no window in which you know the price and the market does not; you are simply reading a press release with extra steps. The only 'edge' would be reading it minutes faster than other retail, which does not matter on a multi-week convergence trade.
triage.already_priced: Heavily. The claim that 13E-3s are 'among the least-watched filing types' is demonstrably false — an entire cottage industry publishes exactly this trade to retail: oddlotarbitrage.com runs a free tracker with a dedicated 'Going Private Transactions' category, oddlotspecialsituations.com sells it as a newsletter, plus reversesplitarbitrage.com, stocksplitarbitrage.com, insidearbitrage.com's reverse-splits page, and reversesplit.substack.com. The stated edge ('structurally uninvestable for funds, perfect for individuals') describes precisely the audience already being served this exact signal for free.
triage.biggest_doubt: Executability at the beneficial-holder level. SIFMA has flagged that reverse-split rounding/cash-out is applied at the DTCC participant level, and issuers only 'instruct' nominees to effect the split for beneficial holders — brokers may apply their own procedures and in some cases keep the round-up on their aggregate position rather than passing it to individual accounts. So the payoff is not contractually yours; it depends on your broker's back office. Combine that with a threshold that caps the position at a few thousand dollars of gross spread, wide bid/ask on illiquid controlled micro-caps, multi-month timetables, re-cut ratios, and deal abandonment leaving you stuck in an unlisted shell — and the risk-adjusted return does not survive.
triage.reason: The data source is genuine and free, but this is a published-price convergence trade with zero informational lead and it is already a productized retail strategy with multiple free public trackers. Position size is structurally capped in the low thousands while the downside is an illiquid controlled micro-cap, and the cash-out is not even reliably passed through to street-name holders. Kills on 'already a commercial product' and 'implied move too small to be worth it.'

triage.name: Rotor Count (Gulf of Mexico crew-helicopter ADS-B)
triage.data_exists: PARTIALLY, and not in the form the idea needs. FAA tail registries and BOEM platform coordinates are public, and Bristow/PHI do operate large GoM fleets. But the FAA's Gulf ADS-B network is a government ATC surveillance system built on receivers mounted on oil platforms — it is not a public feed. Public trackers (ADS-B Exchange, FlightAware) run on ~20,000 volunteer ground receivers with roughly 250 nm line-of-sight range, essentially all coastal. Low-altitude helicopter traffic 100-200 nm offshore to deepwater helidecks is exactly the regime the FAA built the platform network for BECAUSE nothing else sees it. FAA/MIT-LL documentation also notes platform receivers must be physically relocated when a platform is shut in — so coverage degrades precisely during the shut-in events you want to measure. The idea's own 'risk' section concedes this and then proceeds anyway.
triage.latency: Backwards. Evacuations are triggered by the National Hurricane Center's public forecast cone, which the market sees days before any helicopter lifts off. Crew movements are DOWNSTREAM of already-public information, not upstream of it. BSEE also publishes shut-in and platform-evacuation percentages daily at 2:00 p.m. ET during storms (verified across Ida, Laura, Delta, Zeta, Ian, Helene, Rafael releases), and operators issue their own evacuation press releases.
triage.already_priced: Completely. Storm-driven GoM risk premium is one of the most-watched setups in energy — NHC advisories every 6 hours, operator PR, BSEE dailies. There is no plausible world where a retail helicopter counter learns something the NG/CL pits have not already discounted from the public forecast track.
triage.biggest_doubt: The stated mechanism is arithmetically dead for the headline instrument. EIA puts Federal Offshore Gulf gas at ~1.72 Bcf/d in 2025, about 1% of US marketed production (down from 9% in 2010). A total GoM gas shut-in is a rounding error against ~105 Bcf/d of supply — Henry Hub does not 'mechanically move' on it. Crude is somewhat more material (~14% of US output) but WTI is a globally priced barrel and shut-ins last days. Add that the tradeable event count is a handful of storms per year, and offshore ADS-B coverage fails during exactly those storms.
triage.reason: The collection premise fails — public crowd-sourced ADS-B does not cover low-altitude deepwater GoM, and the FAA network that does is not public. Even granting perfect data, GoM gas is ~1% of US supply so the Henry Hub mechanism does not exist, and evacuations follow the public NHC cone, meaning the signal trails the market rather than leading it. A few events a year, all of them already saturated.

triage.name: Upset Detector (TCEQ emission-event filings + PurpleAir)
triage.data_exists: YES. The TCEQ Air Emission Event Report database is real and public (www2.tceq.texas.gov/oce/eer/), searchable by incident number, regulated entity, date range and county, with Excel export; reporting is required under 30 TAC 101.201/101.211. It is genuinely a clunky ColdFusion state web app — the search endpoint threw a server error when I fetched it, which tells you something about scraping it on a 15-minute loop. PurpleAir's API is also real.
