triage.latency: Negative, twice over. (a) The filing lags the physical event: in the ExxonMobil Beaumont case the FCC upset occurred early Tuesday and the TCEQ filing appeared Wednesday. (b) Publication lags the filing by minutes, not hours, because the wires are already parsing it — which is the fatal part.
triage.already_priced: Yes, and this is the decisive finding. OPIS, a Dow Jones company whose content runs on Dow Jones Newswires, systematically monitors TCEQ filings and publishes headlines explicitly tagged as such: 'ExxonMobil's Beaumont, Texas, Refinery Reports Unit Upset : TCEQ Filing -- OPIS' and 'Motiva, Phillips 66 and Valero Report Upsets at Texas Refineries -- OPIS'. S&P Global Platts does the same ('Dow Chemical reports emissions event from PE unit startup at Freeport, Texas: TCEQ'). The idea's core edge claim — that 'the raw upstream regulatory exhaust goes largely unwatched in real time' while only IIR phone surveys are productized — is factually wrong. The exact named source is an established, automated commercial newswire product feeding every energy trading desk.
triage.biggest_doubt: Even if you somehow beat OPIS's crawler by a few minutes, you then need to (a) correctly size the unit from a filing that reports pounds of contaminants rather than barrels of capacity, using a hand-built unit ontology, and (b) trade RBOB/ULSD cracks — a two-leg futures spread with real margin and slippage — on a signal where most events are immaterial flaring noise. The false-positive rate swamps a minutes-scale lead.
triage.reason: The database exists and is public, but the premise that it is unwatched is false: OPIS/Dow Jones and S&P Platts already run automated TCEQ-filing monitors and push headlines to the wire. The filing itself also trails the physical unit trip by 12-36 hours, so refinery-town scanners, IIR and Reuters routinely have it first. No informational lead survives.

triage.name: Channel Fog (LNG-channel met-ocean halts)
triage.data_exists: PARTIALLY. NDBC realtime data and NWS marine dense-fog advisories are public APIs/feeds. But the buoy leg is weak — visibility is not a standard NDBC sensor on most Gulf buoys, so the actual closure decision is not observable from buoy data. The real signal is the pilot associations' boarding suspensions, and those are not obscure: they are republished in near-real time by GAC Hot Port News ('Channel closures due to fog'), Moran Shipping port bulletins, and RSSA maritime updates, with exact timestamps (e.g. Houston Ship Channel closed 0425 Dec 12; closed 1730 Dec 20; outbound-only 1725 Feb 19 to 0900 Feb 20).
triage.latency: Effectively none. Fog closures are a covered news beat, not a data-collection problem. Natural Gas Intelligence ran 'Vessel Traffic Limited at Sabine Pass LNG by Heavy Fog Forecast Through Weekend' — note 'forecast,' i.e. the trade-relevant news is published BEFORE the closure. S&P Global Platts covers the tanker queues live. The idea's own risk section concedes feedgas nominations compress the lead to hours; in reality the marine-agency and gas-trade press are ahead of the closure itself.
triage.already_priced: Yes. LNG tanker movements are a mature commercial product (AIS-based cargo tracking from Kpler/Vortexa/Bloomberg), daily feedgas nominations are scraped off pipeline EBBs by every gas desk and reported by NGI/Argus, and fog forecasts are NWS public output that gas traders already read. 'Almost nobody systematizes winter fog closures' is not credible when three trade publications and multiple shipping agencies cover each one.
triage.biggest_doubt: Magnitude. In the 2021 Sabine Pass fog episode — a multi-day event severe enough that tankers visibly backed up outside the channel — feedgas fell about 400 MMcf/d off a ~4 Bcf/d base. That is roughly 0.4% of ~105 Bcf/d US supply, arriving as a known, forecast, days-long, mean-reverting blip that terminals partially absorb via tank inventory and berth re-sequencing. Front-month Henry Hub routinely moves several percent on a weather-model run; this signal is buried far below that noise floor, and you would be paying futures/options spread to harvest it.
triage.reason: Data is real but the 'obscure maritime channel' framing is wrong — pilot suspensions are republished within minutes by GAC, Moran and RSSA, and NGI/Platts/Argus cover fog impacts on LNG loadings, often from the forecast stage. The physical effect is ~0.4 Bcf/d against ~105 Bcf/d, too small and too well-telegraphed to trade against Henry Hub's weather-driven volatility.

triage.name: Wallet-Freeze Basis Trade
triage.data_exists: Yes, but not obtainable by this trader. GET /sapi/v1/capital/config/getall is documented (developers.binance.com/docs/wallet/capital) and returns per-network depositEnable/withdrawEnable, with depositDesc/withdrawDesc populated only when false. However it is an HMAC-signed endpoint requiring a Binance.com account, and Binance.com blocks US persons; Binance.US is a legally separate entity offering spot only, no perps, no margin. So both the primary feed AND the perp leg of the named trade are closed to a US small trader.
triage.latency: Negative — the feed LAGS the news. Binance pre-announces the overwhelming majority of suspensions days in advance with exact UTC start times ('Binance Will Support the X Network Upgrade & Hard Fork'), and those notices are syndicated within minutes by CryptoRank, CryptoPanic, BitcoinWorld and Followin. The config flag flips after the public announcement, so polling it every minute is lagging confirmation of already-published news. Binance's own notices also state trading is unaffected during these windows.
triage.already_priced: Yes. Cross-venue arbitrage scanners (ArbitrageScanner and peers, 80+ CEXs, sub-second refresh) already surface withdrawal-network status, matching withdrawal networks and fees as headline features, because deposit/withdrawal state determines whether an arb can be closed at all. This is table stakes for crypto market makers, not an unwatched corner.
triage.reason: The flags are real but arrive after Binance's own scheduled-maintenance announcements, so there is no informational lead on the benign events. The only unannounced flips are the hack/insolvency cases the idea itself identifies as adverse selection — picking up pennies in front of a collapse. Separately, the named venue and instrument are both inaccessible to a US small trader.
triage.biggest_doubt: Whether some genuinely unscheduled freeze on a mid-cap token throws a tradeable premium before any announcement posts. Even granting that, you would be fading a freeze whose cause you cannot diagnose, on a venue you cannot legally access, against desks that already monitor withdrawal state as a core input.

triage.name: Sponsor-Read Ledger
triage.data_exists: Yes, and it is genuinely free. SponsorBlock publishes DB dumps at sponsor.ajay.app/database (JSON index; CSV disabled for bandwidth) with community mirrors refreshing every 10-90 minutes (sb.ltn.fi, mirror.sb.mchang.xyz, sb.minibomba.pro) plus an sb-mirror incremental fetch tool. The data source is the one part of this idea that checks out.
triage.latency: Timing is not the binding constraint — sponsor reads publish as videos go live, weeks ahead of the reported marketing-expense line. The failure is in signal content, not clock: influencer sponsorship is a small, noisy slice of these issuers' customer-acquisition spend, and multi-brand reads plus ambiguous coupon codes wreck attribution, as the idea concedes.
triage.already_priced: Yes, decisively — the central edge claim is factually false. The transcript-joined sponsorship panel is an off-the-shelf commercial product from multiple vendors: YTSponsorDB markets 1M+ tracked video ad reads across 10K sponsors with full transcripts and proprietary valuations; SponsorRadar indexes ~972,000 sponsorships across 66,000 brands and 65,000 channels; SponsorTrack detects sponsorships and estimates spend across YouTube, podcasts and newsletters; Gospel Stats publishes a recurring YouTube Sponsorship Landscape Report. 'Nobody has joined it to transcripts' is simply wrong.
triage.reason: Kill on two independent grounds. First, the dataset-join that constitutes the entire edge is a commoditized commercial category with at least four vendors selling it. Second, half the named trade universe is untradeable: Squarespace (SQSP) was taken private by Permira and delisted from the NYSE in October 2024, and HelloFresh (HFG.DE) is Frankfurt-listed with no practical US retail options market — leaving DKNG and DUOL keyed to a minor fraction of their marketing spend.
triage.biggest_doubt: Whether view-weighted sponsor-read share for a single brand carries any incremental information about new-customer adds once you subtract what the existing vendors already disseminate. At a 2-6 week horizon into earnings, against consensus, I doubt it clears the noise floor.

triage.name: Roblox Live Census
triage.data_exists: Yes. games.roblox.com/v1/games returns live per-universe 'playing' counts with no authentication, and third parties poll it continuously. Rate limits exist and are not published per-endpoint, which makes a 2,000-ID census every 10 minutes an engineering nuisance rather than a blocker.
triage.latency: The telemetry is real-time, but one of the two named trade legs does not exist. Roblox announced in March 2023 that it would cease monthly key-metrics reporting to align with its quarterly cadence, with the final monthly release in April 2023. There are no monthly-metrics releases to trade around; disclosure is quarterly only.
triage.already_priced: Yes — the signal IS the consensus. RoMonitor Stats already publishes platform-wide peak CCU sampled at half-hourly intervals across tracked experiences, for free. Citi has published research citing RoMonitor average peak CCU (15.3M, down 5% y/y), and RBLX fell roughly 8% on that CCU commentary. The nowcast reaches the entire buy side through sell-side notes faster than a self-built census would reach one small trader.
triage.reason: The edge claim — that institutions buy panel data while nobody bothers to run the platform's own telemetry — is refuted by a free public tracker whose numbers already move the stock through published analyst notes. You would be rebuilding the consensus dataset and receiving it later than anyone reading the Citi note, while the monthly-release leg of the trade was discontinued in 2023.
triage.biggest_doubt: Whether monetization-tier weighting adds enough over RoMonitor's headline CCU to beat consensus bookings. Even if it did, the risk the idea names — an engagement-flat but monetization-hot quarter — is exactly where a CCU integral breaks, and that is the quarter that would decide the P&L.

triage.name: Cooling-Off Clock (NMB/FMCS Strike Countdown)
triage.data_exists: Partially, and weaker than described. NMB does publish determinations, dockets and press releases at nmb.gov. The FMCS leg is degraded: FMCS publishes only some F-7 spreadsheets, and the Data Liberation Project's FOIA for the full F-7 database was largely withheld under claimed mediation privilege and confidential commercial/financial exemptions. What is public is already scraped and republished on GitHub (labordata/fmcs-f7). FMCS also shed roughly 95% of staff after the March 2025 'Continuing the Reduction of The Federal Bureaucracy' executive order, closing regional offices and cancelling mediations.
triage.latency: Zero lead. NMB issues a public press release announcing the cooling-off period as it begins — e.g. the LIRR/BLET-BRS-IAMAW-IBEW-TCU release on 8/18/2025 with the cooling-off period starting 8/19/2025 and the NMB press release dated 8/19/2025 — while the unions and carriers announce simultaneously to members and the wires. Airline and rail labor disputes are covered by mainstream outlets in real time.
triage.already_priced: Yes. The release-from-mediation date is a publicly announced, precisely dated catalyst known to every airline analyst and options desk the same day it happens. The claim that desks 'only price the risk after a strike-authorization vote' is backwards — authorization votes are themselves heavily publicized news events, not private information.
triage.reason: Kill on informational lead, not tradeability. The instruments are genuinely liquid and optionable (AAL, UAL, LUV, UNP, CSX, NSC), but NMB press-releases the statutory clock the day it starts, so there is nothing to front-run. The payoff base rate compounds the problem: the last nationwide rail strike was 1991 and Congress ended it in under 24 hours, and PEBs plus congressional intervention routinely pre-empt stoppages — so this is dated premium bought against a near-zero-probability binary that implied vol already reflects.
triage.biggest_doubt: Whether a hand-built amendable-date calendar could flag months ahead which disputes will actually reach release, before the docket makes it obvious. That might be a real edge — but it is a slower, different trade than the one specified here, whose stated entry trigger is a government press release.

referee.name: Call Report Amendment Autopsy
referee.edge_case: The informational asymmetry is REAL and verified — it is the economic content that is absent. Confirmed true: (1) The FFIEC CDR web service exists and is pullable daily; `RetrieveFilersSubmissionDateTime` returns RSSD IDs + submission timestamps for filers since a given datetime, which is a purpose-built, cheap amendment detector (spec CDR-PDD-SIS-611 v1.10; ~2,500 req/hr limit; free registration, 90-day JWT, no refresh token). (2) Amendments genuinely erase history. Badertscher/Burks/Easton state it outright: "the process of amending reports erases historical data and provides no indication of which items were amended," and "SNL Financial overwrites its record of the original filing when there is an amendment." So versioned diffing does require you to snapshot yourself. (3) Amendments trigger no 8-K, no press release, no newswire. (4) Amendments are frequent: 36.29% of Call Reports amended within 3 months of quarter-end (n=970 of 2,673 firm-quarters, 319 publicly traded BHCs, 2012Q1–2014Q1). (5) RI-E free-text itemization is real — banks must name and size the three largest "other noninterest expense" components exceeding 10% of RI item 7.c, so litigation/settlement strings do appear. (6) There IS one documented real effect nearby: on original Day-30 Call Report release, mean (median) RET is 7.3% (9.5%) higher than non-event days, and in ~19% of bank-quarters the Call Report precedes the earnings release (median 6 days, mean 11 days), concentrated in smaller banks (median assets $1.1B vs $2.1B).
referee.against_case: Three independent, individually fatal problems. FIRST — the exact event has been directly tested and produces nothing. Badertscher, Burks & Easton, "The Market Reaction to Bank Regulatory Reports," Review of Accounting Studies 23(2), 2018 (DOI 10.1007/s11142-018-9440-8), built precisely the proposed pipeline: they downloaded filings DAILY in real time specifically to capture originals and subsequent amendments. Table 2 Panel B, on 758 clean amendments (excluding any coinciding with an EA, Y-9C, or 10-K/Q): RET mean 1.159 on amendment days vs 1.171 on 156,941 non-event days, difference −0.0122; VOL 1.28409 vs 1.39594, difference −0.1119. RET is |market-adjusted 2-day return| normalized to the bank's own prior-quarter baseline (≈1.0 on a normal day). Amendment days are ~1% LESS volatile and ~8% LOWER volume than a random day. Not a weak positive — a null with a slightly negative point estimate. SECOND — the stated MECHANISM is arithmetically false. The claim is that the amendment "front-runs the 10-Q." Time from original to amended Call Report: mean 22.18 days, median 19, Q1 11, Q3 33. Originals cluster on day 30, so the median amendment lands ~day 49. The 10-Q is due day 40 (accelerated/large accelerated) or day 45 (non-accelerated) — verified. The median amendment therefore arrives AFTER the 10-Q it is supposed to precede; only roughly the first quartile beats a 45-day filer, and almost none beat a 40-day filer. THIRD — no taxonomy can rescue it, because the underlying revisions are numerically empty. Only 114/970 amendments (11.8%) change total assets at all, mean change $2.95M = 0.158% of assets (median 0.042%). Only 198/970 (20.4%) change the Tier 1 ratio, mean 21bp, MEDIAN 6bp, Q3 21bp. There is no fat adverse tail to filter toward. Bonus kill on the fallback: even for CALL1 events (Call Report precedes earnings — the strongest possible version of this trade) BBE find "volume reaction but no price reaction." And the Day-30 effect that does exist is crowded: an early draft "was covered in the business press and promoted to investor clients of SNL Financial and Barclays," after which the authors measured the market reaction becoming MORE pronounced. Also, the universe is overstated — ~428 publicly traded US banks/thrifts reported Q4 2024 (Capital Performance Group/S&P), and other counts run ~600, not 700. Finally, RI-E's 10%-of-other-noninterest-expense trigger is a LOW bar: for a $1B bank that is roughly a $200k item, so free-text strings fire constantly on amounts immaterial to earnings — a high-false-positive generator, not a sparse alarm.
referee.who_is_on_other_side: Nobody informed — which is exactly the problem, not the opportunity. The measured VOL difference of −0.1119 on amendment days means these events pass with BELOW-average trading volume: the market does not react because there is nothing to react to. You are not picking off an informed seller. Your actual counterparty is (a) the market maker quoting a 1–5% wide spread in a $17k–$31k/day microcap bank, who collects that spread with certainty regardless of whether your thesis is right, and (b) buy-and-hold retail/local/ESOP/thrift-conversion holders of community bank stock who will never see, and would not trade on, a $200k expense reclassification. The market maker is the only reliable winner in this trade. On the adjacent Day-30 original-filing leg the counterparty is different and much better informed: SNL/S&P Capital IQ subscribers, Barclays clients, and quant desks who have been explicitly told about this effect since roughly 2015 and whose entry BBE document as having INCREASED the reaction.
referee.frictions: Verified name-level data for the target cohort ($200M–$2B assets → ~$40–300M market cap), priced 12 Aug 2026: MBBC (Marathon Bancorp) $14.16 × 1,179 sh ADV = ~$16,700/day dollar volume, $41.8M cap. CPBI (Central Plains Bancshares) $20.97 × 1,486 sh = ~$31,200/day, $81.7M cap. Also FSEA 1,732 sh/day, CLST 7,514, TCBS 3,540, NSTS 4,908, KFFB 17,035. COST STACK, target microcap names, round trip: bid-ask 1–5% of price typical for microcaps (assume 2% quoted → ~2% round trip paying the spread both ways); market impact 2–5% — a $50k short is 1.6–3.0x TOTAL daily dollar volume in MBBC/CPBI, and at a disciplined 10%-of-ADV participation rate a $50k position in CPBI takes 16 trading days to build, longer than the entire 1–6 week holding period; commissions negligible ($0–0.005/sh) but HTB locate fees $25–100 flat/per-locate matter on a $10k position; borrow is the binding constraint — these are recent thrift conversions with heavy insider/ESOP ownership and near-zero lendable institutional float, so borrow is frequently simply unavailable at any price, and where locatable HTB microcaps run 5–50%+ annualized (≈0.3–3% for a 1–6 week hold); options do not exist at these market caps, so there is no defined-risk route — only the ~150 largest listed banks have listed options, and there spreads run 5–15% of premium with IV bid up into earnings. TOTAL round trip in target names: ~4–10%. In the liquid tail ($1B+ cap, real borrow): ~30–60bp spread+impact plus 0.3–1% borrow, so ~0.4–1.2% — but that is precisely where the measured edge is zero and coverage is thick. KRE hedge itself is cheap (1–2bp spread, deep ADV) but does not help: it strips market beta while leaving 3-week idiosyncratic vol of a single community bank at ~8–15%, roughly 10x any plausible signal.
referee.capacity: Effectively zero — low tens of thousands of dollars per event, which is below the threshold where the strategy pays for its own infrastructure. At a 10%-of-ADV participation cap, MBBC absorbs ~$1,700/day and CPBI ~$3,100/day, so building and exiting a position inside a 1–6 week window caps you around $8k–$30k per name. Across ~1–3 mechanism-intact events per year, annual gross notional deployed is ~$25k–$100k; stretching to all ~5–8 borrowable-name events gets you to maybe $0.5–1.5M of annual gross notional only if you relax into larger, well-covered banks where the edge is measured at zero. Even granting a hypothetical (entirely unproven) 100bp gross edge, that is $250–$15,000 of gross P&L per year against a 4–10% friction drag — i.e., the position sizes at which the trade is theoretically viable are smaller than the cost of the data engineering, and the position sizes worth engineering for do not exist in these names. Borrow availability, not capital, is the first hard stop.
referee.net_edge_estimate: Negative, and the sign is not close. Measured gross edge on the exact event is 0.00% — BBE's n=758 clean-amendment test gives RET difference −0.0122 and VOL difference −0.1119, a tight null with a slightly negative point estimate. Against that: 4–10% round-trip friction in the target microcap universe, or 0.4–1.2% in the liquid tail. Net expectancy per trade: roughly −2% to −10% in the names the idea actually targets, and −0.5% to −1.5% in names you can actually short. Now the statistical kill, which matters more than the cost kill: even if you generously assume the pooled null masks a real +100bp drift in some adverse subset, 3-week idiosyncratic vol of a community bank is ~10%, so per-trade signal-to-noise is 0.01/0.10 = 0.10. At ~6 events/year the standalone annual Sharpe of the RAW signal before any costs is 0.10 × √6 ≈ 0.25, implying you would need ~60–70 years of live trading to distinguish this from zero at conventional significance. You cannot ever learn whether it works, and you pay 4–10% per attempt to find out. Event funnel: ~500 listed banks × 4 quarters × 36.3% ≈ 700–750 raw amendments/year → ~150/year that touch total assets or Tier 1 at all → ~15–25/year with a Tier 1 change above 50bp → ~5–8/year of those in names with borrow and a tradeable spread → ~1–3/year that ALSO land before the 10-Q with the stated mechanism intact.
referee.event_frequency: ~700–750 raw amendments/year across the ~428–600 exchange-listed US bank universe (extrapolating BBE's verified 36.29% three-month amendment rate). But the tradeable funnel collapses hard: ~150/year alter total assets or the Tier 1 ratio at all (11.8% and 20.4% respectively); ~15–25/year carry a Tier 1 change above 50bp; ~5–8/year of those occur in names with locatable borrow and a sub-1% spread; and only ~1–3/year additionally arrive BEFORE the 10-Q so that the stated front-running mechanism is even intact. One to three mechanism-intact events per year is far below the rate at which any edge could be validated or could amortize the build.
referee.data_pipeline: FFIEC CDR Public Data Distribution web service (https://cdr.ffiec.gov/public/pws/webservices/retrievalservice.asmx; spec CDR-PDD-SIS-611 v1.10). Free registration via FFIEC portal → Microsoft Entra ID, 90-day JWT bearer token with NO refresh-token support (manual regeneration every 90 days, a real operational failure mode for an unattended daily job). Rate limit ~2,500 requests/hour. Poll `RetrieveFilersSubmissionDateTime` daily per reporting period to detect resubmissions (returns RSSD + submission datetime for filers since a given datetime), then `RetrieveFacsimile` to pull the current version and diff against your own archive — the API exposes only the latest version, so all version history must be self-generated from day one, meaning the strategy has ZERO backtestable history and requires 2–3 years of forward archiving before you have even the ~1–3/yr events needed to begin evaluating it. Cadence: originals cluster tightly on day 30 after quarter-end (35 for the few banks with foreign offices); amendments arrive continuously, mean 22.2 / median 19 days after the original, with 46% of them in the first 16 days post-release, driven largely by FDIC analyst review rather than by bank-discovered problems. Newswire/company release: yes, it beats you — earnings announcements precede the Call Report in ~81% of bank-quarters. Cross-reference needs: SEC EDGAR for 10-Q/8-K dates, CRSP/vendor for ADV and borrow, FDIC Summary of Deposits to map RSSD → holding company → ticker. Note the claimed vendor gap is narrower than stated: bankregreports.com advertises syncing FFIEC filings "including late amendments," so at least partial amendment ingestion exists commercially even if original-vs-amended diffs are not exposed.
referee.confidence: HIGH — unusually high for a negative verdict, because this is not an inference from priors but a direct hit. The exact event (Call Report amendments), on the exact universe (publicly traded BHCs), collected by the exact proposed method (daily real-time snapshotting to catch originals vs. amendments), was tested in a peer-reviewed accounting journal (Review of Accounting Studies, 2018) with n=758 clean events, and returned a precise null with a slightly negative point estimate. The timing refutation is arithmetic, not statistical: median amendment at ~day 49 vs a day-40/45 10-Q deadline, both independently verified. The liquidity refutation is verified at name level with live quotes. VERIFIED: the RAST paper and all its statistics (extracted from the authors' full working-paper text, not a summary); 10-Q deadlines (40/45 days); FFIEC API methods, auth model, and rate limits; RI-E 10% itemization threshold; live price/ADV for MBBC, CPBI, FSEA, CLST, TCBS, NSTS, KFFB; listed-bank universe counts. UNVERIFIED / FLAGGED: the 36.29% amendment base rate is from 2012Q1–2014Q1 and a benign credit period — I did not confirm it for 2026, and a stress regime could plausibly carry more signal (though 2023's RC-O uninsured-deposit lines are already crowded, as the triage notes concede); I had no market-data terminal, so name-level borrow availability and locate rates are inferred from general HTB literature rather than actual broker locate screens; options availability on specific microcap banks was not directly confirmed (inferred from market cap); I did not independently replicate BBE on recent data; and whether any vendor now exposes true original-vs-amended diffs remains unconfirmed in both directions. None of these caveats can plausibly overturn the verdict, because the timing and liquidity kills are independent of the empirical null — each is separately fatal.

referee.name: Dividend Clock Slip
referee.edge_case:
The honest case, stated at its strongest:

1. The underlying statistical relationship is real and peer-reviewed. Onali, "Can we predict dividend cuts?", Economics Letters vol. 146 (2016), pp. 71-76, US firms 1971-2014: "The longer the time interval between dividend announcements, the larger the probability of a cut in the dividend per share, consistent with the view that firms delay the release of bad news." (NOTE: the brainstorm cites this as Journal of Corporate Finance 2016 — that is a misattribution. Journal/volume verified via RePEc and ScienceDirect listing.)

2. The latency argument is genuinely sound. You are trading an inference from an absence, so no newswire can beat you to the tape. There is no publication race. This is a real structural property and it distinguishes the idea from most event-driven screens.

3. The sector stress is real. Median US-listed BDC dividend coverage of 0.99x, falling to 0.89x ex-PIK (Q1 2026) is corroborated, and real cuts are landing: MRCC -64%, TPVG -43% cumulative since Q2 2024, TWO -13% then further to $0.34. Conditional on a genuine surprise cut, -10% to -25% single-session in this cohort is a fair estimate.

4. Capacity is so small that no institution has an incentive to compete it away — the one favorable consequence of the microcap universe.

That is where the case ends. Every load-bearing operational premise below it failed verification.
referee.against_case:
Four independent failures, any one of which is close to disqualifying.

**(1) The "hidden per-board baseline" does not exist — declaration dates are publicly pre-announced.** For BDCs, the core of the named universe, the distribution is declared inside the earnings release, and the earnings release date is announced 1-3 weeks ahead in a dedicated scheduling press release. Verified: Crescent Capital BDC issued its scheduling release 2026-07-24 for an 2026-08-10 release; Goldman Sachs BDC issued 2026-04-14 for 2026-05-07. There is no archival baseline to reconstruct — the company publishes the date. Where the schedule shifts, a revised scheduling release goes out. The "absence" is announced, not silent.

**(2) The three flagship examples used to justify the idea all falsify it — the signal would have fired zero times.**
- Two Harbors: Q1-25 dividend declared 2025-03-19 ($0.45); the 13% cut to $0.39 declared 2025-06-18. Both the third Wednesday of the quarter-ending month, exactly one quarter apart. ZERO slip. Cause was a $198.9M litigation contingency accrual (2020 internalization) already publicly disclosed and quantified.
- Monroe Capital: Q4-24 earnings 2025-03-03; Q4-25 earnings plus the 64% cut to $0.09 on 2026-03-05. Two days of year-over-year drift. On cadence. Also confounded — MRCC is being absorbed by HRZN, so the cut is entangled with merger consideration.
- Blue Owl (OBDC) similarly cut its base dividend to $0.31 in the scheduled Q1-26 earnings release.
Observed hit rate of this specific screen on the specific events cited as proof: 0 for 3.

**(3) There is a mechanical reason for (2), which generalizes.** For a RIC/BDC or REIT the dividend is an arithmetic output of net investment income and the 90% distribution requirement. It is produced by the same quarter-close process that produces the earnings number — not by a separate contentious board meeting that can run long. The premise that the declaration gap is "the observable shadow of internal debate" is a plausible story for industrials with discretionary payouts; it is largely false for exactly the high-yield RIC/REIT complex the trade targets.

**(4) The remaining cohorts are structurally excluded.** Monthly payers pre-declare in blocks — Prospect Capital declares three months at once (record dates 2025-11-25, 2025-12-29, 2026-01-28 declared together), so no window can lapse until the block expires, by which point deterioration is fully public. And when a corporate calendar genuinely slips, the company files Form 12b-25 (NT 10-Q/NT 10-K) on EDGAR stating the reason — a hard, timestamped, universally-screened affirmative disclosure. In the one case where the delay is real and severe, you have no lead at all.

**(5) The "no commercial feed" claim is false.** Dividend declaration date is a standard field in CRSP, Compustat, Bloomberg (DVD_DECLARED_DT), FactSet and Refinitiv. TWO's third-Wednesday rule is derivable from a free stockanalysis.com table in under a minute. Confusing "not productized as a retail screen" with "not known" is the central error. A relationship published in 1986 and again in 2016 on standard vendor fields is not obscure.

**(6) Pre-pricing eliminates the residual.** TPVG trades at 0.62x NAV on a 17% yield with 3.7% non-accruals. At that valuation a cut is consensus, not news. Cuts in pre-discounted names often produce single-digit or positive reactions — CCAP fell only 2.05% after its dividend announcement. The -10/-25% figure is a selected sample of the worst cases.

**(7) The false-positive tail is violent.** "Late but intact" is by far the most common resolution, and it produces a relief rally in a heavily-shorted 17%-yield name. Shorting a 0.62x-NAV BDC into a dividend confirmation can cost 8-15% in a session.
referee.who_is_on_other_side:
Two distinct populations, and the idea misidentifies which one sets the price.

**The population the thesis assumes:** yield-reaching retail income investors who watch amounts and ex-dates, not declaration timestamps. These holders are real and they genuinely do not monitor per-board cadence. But they are the marginal price-setter in the fat, healthy, uncontroversial payers — precisely the names where no cut is coming and the signal never fires.

**The population that actually sets the price in a flagged name:** credit-focused hedge funds and specialist BDC/mREIT analysts who read the same non-accrual tables, PIK ratios and NAV marks in the 10-Q that you do. In a name trading at 0.62x NAV with 0.89x ex-PIK coverage, these are the marginal participants — and the elevated borrow cost is the direct evidence they are already short. You are not front-running naive income holders; you are queuing behind informed credit money that got there on fundamentals months earlier.

Also on the other side: the BDC's external manager, who frequently buys back stock at a discount to NAV (often authorized precisely during distress, exactly when you are short); index and passive high-yield flows; and dividend-capture funds accumulating into the ex-date, which is the mechanism that makes the "late but intact" squeeze so sharp.
referee.frictions:
Priced on TPVG ($5.41, ~$200M cap, 17.0% yield, 0.62x NAV) and MRCC (~$150M cap) as representative flagged names. Spread and options figures are ESTIMATED from price/cap/strike structure — MarketChameleon required login and I could not directly observe live quotes. Flagged as unverified.

**Equity short, 3-week hold:**
- Bid-ask: $0.01-0.03 on a $5.41 stock = 0.2-0.6% round trip.
- Slippage/impact: 0.2-0.5% on a $200M-cap name at retail size; materially worse above ~$250k.
- Borrow: these fit the "small cap, heavy short interest" profile that sources put in double-digit annualized territory; 10-40% annualized = 0.6-2.3% for three weeks. Verified only as a general range (0.25% easy-to-borrow to 100%+ hard-to-borrow), not name-by-name. The distressed names are the ones most likely to be unborrowable exactly when the flag fires.
- Commissions: negligible at retail (~$0).
- **Dividend liability — the structural killer.** If the resolution is "late but intact," the declaration typically carries an ex-date 1-2 weeks later. TPVG pays $0.23/quarter on $5.41 = 4.25% per quarter owed to the lender if caught over ex-date. Avoidable only by covering into the relief rally at the worst available price. On a 15-20% yielder this single item can exceed the entire theoretical edge.
- **Equity-short round trip: ~1.5-3.5% before any dividend accident.**

**Puts — not viable:**
- A $5.41 underlying has $2.50/$5.00/$7.50 strikes. A 1-2 month ATM put realistically quotes ~$0.15 bid / $0.35 ask: a 40-60% round-trip spread as a fraction of mid.
- Open interest on small-BDC options is routinely single- to double-digit contracts; many strikes are quoteless or one-sided.
- You must be right on direction, magnitude AND timing — the 1-3 week resolution window has to land inside your expiry.
- **Options round trip: 20-50% of premium.** A signal worth a few hundred basis points cannot survive this. The options expression of this trade is dead on arrival.
referee.capacity:
$1-3M total deployed capital, optimistically, and borrow availability rather than liquidity is the binding constraint.

Per-name: $50k-250k short without meaningful impact in $150-250M-cap names with thin volume. Spraying across 30-60 flags/year to catch 3-10 real events implies most capital sits in false positives.

Options capacity is effectively nil — single- to double-digit open interest means even a 20-contract order is the entire book.

For a small trader capacity is not the binding constraint, and the microcap floor is the one genuinely favorable feature: it explains why no institution has bothered to compete this away. But it also means the strategy can never scale beyond a personal account, and the borrow constraint bites hardest on exactly the distressed names where the signal has any content.
referee.net_edge_estimate:
Negative to break-even for equities; decisively negative for options.

Generous parameterization: p(cut | tight flag) = 0.20; conditional move -15% (already generous given pre-pricing); so +3.0% gross on winners. p(no cut) = 0.80 with an average -1.5% against you (mixing flat outcomes with occasional -8/-15% relief squeezes) = -1.2%. **Gross expectancy ~ +1.8% per trade.**

Subtract equity-short friction of 1.5-3.5% (excluding dividend accidents): **net -1.7% to +0.3% per trade**, centered negative. Add any dividend liability event and it is clearly negative.

Via puts: a 20-50% premium haircut against a gross edge of ~180bp is unambiguously negative. No parameterization rescues it.

And p(cut | flag) = 0.20 is almost certainly too high. The measured evidence points the other way: on the three cut events cited as the idea's live proof, the screen fires 0 for 3, because all three cuts were declared on schedule inside pre-announced earnings releases.

Annualized, at 3-10 events/year and $50-250k per position, even the optimistic tail of the range produces a few thousand dollars of gross P&L against real borrow bills, tail squeeze risk in illiquid names, and substantial operational effort.
referee.confidence:
Moderate-to-high on the verdict; the structural findings are directly verified and mutually reinforcing.

**Directly verified:** Onali (2016) journal/volume/pages/sample/finding (RePEc, ScienceDirect listing). BDC earnings-date pre-announcement practice (Crescent 2026-07-24 scheduling release for 2026-08-10; Goldman Sachs BDC 2026-04-14 for 2026-05-07). TWO declaration dates 2025-03-19 and 2025-06-18 and the $198.9M litigation accrual rationale (company IR press release). MRCC earnings dates 2025-03-03 and 2026-03-05 and the $0.09 declaration (SEC 8-K exhibits, GlobeNewswire). PSEC three-month block pre-declaration (8-K/StockTitan). TPVG price $5.41, $200M cap, 17.0% yield, 0.62x NAV, 3.7% non-accruals. Existence and function of Form 12b-25/NT 10-Q.

**Explicitly unverified — flagged, not asserted:**
- Onali's effect sizes, marginal effects and predictive accuracy. Both ScienceDirect and the Exeter repository returned HTTP 403. The direction of the finding is confirmed; its MAGNITUDE is not. This matters — the paper could be reporting a statistically significant but economically trivial effect.
- Kalay & Loewenstein (1986). NOT independently verified in this review. Treat the brainstorm's characterization as unconfirmed.
- Name-specific borrow fees for TPVG/MRCC. Only general market ranges confirmed.
- Live options quotes and open interest for TPVG/MRCC. Estimated from price/cap/strike structure, not observed.
- The 0.99x / 0.89x ex-PIK coverage figures: corroborated on a single secondary source for Q1 2026, not traced to a primary sector aggregator.
- Event frequency (3-10/yr) is MY estimate. I found no published base rate for late dividend declarations in this universe, and no dataset. That absence is itself a finding: the idea's central quantity has never been measured, and the proposal offers no way to measure it before risking capital.

**What would change my mind:** a measured base rate showing p(cut | declaration slip) materially above ~35% in a modern (post-2015) high-yield universe AFTER controlling for payout ratio, coverage and NAV discount — i.e. proving the timestamp adds information beyond what commercial dividend-safety screens already price. Also, a narrower universe restricted to payers whose declaration is genuinely decoupled from the earnings calendar (some midstream, some closed-end funds, some foreign-domiciled) would be a fairer test than the BDC complex, which is structurally the worst possible place to run this. Separately, the "silence on forward dividend guidance in an earnings call" tell surfaced during research is closer to a real signal than declaration-date drift — but it is a text-based signal, not this one, and would need evaluating on its own terms.
referee.event_frequency:
3-10 genuinely tradeable events per year — ESTIMATED, not measured; no published base rate exists for this universe and I could not construct one from public sources within this review.

Derivation: ~250 high-yield names across BDCs (~130 listed, many without tradeable options), mREITs (~35-40), midstream (~25) and high-yield REITs/telecom; perhaps 120-150 have any option market at all. A threshold tight enough to avoid drowning in benign calendar drift (holiday shifts, board meetings moved a week, fiscal-calendar changes, merger integration) flags maybe 30-60 names/year. Of those, the share resolving as a cut within 1-3 weeks AND not already priced is perhaps 10-20%.

Three structural deductions shrink this further, and they are the reason the estimate should be read as an upper bound:
- BDCs declaring with pre-announced earnings dates are excluded in principle — the declaration date is published, so nothing is inferred.
- Monthly payers pre-declaring in blocks (PSEC-style) cannot generate a lapsed window.
- Genuine calendar slips severe enough to matter surface as Form 12b-25 filings — public, timestamped, universally screened, no lead.

After also excluding names where the market has already priced the cut (0.6x NAV, high-teens yield), the residual surprise set approaches zero. Empirically, on the three 2025-26 cuts cited as the idea's proof, the screen would have generated zero signals.
referee.data_pipeline:
Buildable and free, but this is precisely what makes the idea unattractive rather than attractive — the barrier the thesis relies on does not exist.

**Sources and cadence:**
- Nasdaq.com dividend history / stockanalysis.com: ex-date, record, pay, amount. Free, daily. Declaration date often ABSENT (stockanalysis.com showed ex-dates only for TWO) — a real gap, since the declaration timestamp is the whole signal.
- SEC EDGAR full-text search + daily index: 8-K Item 8.01 exhibits carry most BDC/REIT dividend releases. Near-real-time (minutes). BUT dividend declarations are NOT a mandatory 8-K item — Item 8.01 is voluntary — so EDGAR coverage is incomplete and inconsistent across issuers. This weakens the proposed pipeline's most authoritative leg.
- Company IR pages / GlobeNewswire / BusinessWire: authoritative and timestamped, but require per-issuer scraping.
- Form 12b-25 (NT 10-K/NT 10-Q) on EDGAR: the genuine "calendar is slipping" event, machine-readable and free — but affirmative public disclosure, so no lead.
- Earnings-date scheduling releases ("X Schedules Earnings Release and Conference Call"), issued 1-3 weeks ahead: these must be ingested, because they overwrite any historical cadence baseline. Ingesting them is what reveals the signal has no content.

**Cadence needed:** daily cron pre-open is sufficient; the resolution window is days-to-weeks, so intraday latency is irrelevant. This confirms the triage note's latency claim — but latency was never the binding constraint.

**The killer:** declaration date is a standard vendor field (CRSP, Compustat, Bloomberg DVD_DECLARED_DT, FactSet, Refinitiv). Any CRSP subscriber can reproduce the entire baseline in a short SQL query. The "tedious archival work with no commercial feed" premise conflates absence of a retail product with absence of knowledge.

redteam.target: Dividend Clock Slip — shorting high-yield BDC/mREIT names (TPVG, MRCC archetype) when the interval since last dividend declaration exceeds its historical cadence, on the Onali (2016) finding that longer inter-announcement intervals predict dividend cuts.

kill_shots.attack: THE LATENCY ARGUMENT IS FACTUALLY BACKWARDS — there is no absence to infer from, because the date is affirmatively published on the wire, and a vendor streams it sub-second. The proponent's single strongest claim ('you trade an inference from an absence, no newswire can beat you to the tape') is false at the level of observable fact, and the proponent's own flagship name is the counterexample. TPVG issues a standalone BusinessWire release titled 'TriplePoint Venture Growth BDC Corp. to Announce 2026 First Quarter Financial Results on Wednesday, May 6, 2026', dated 22 April 2026 — roughly two weeks of advance, timestamped and machine-readable. The same pattern holds sector-wide (Goldman Sachs BDC, Crescent Capital BDC, Kayne Anderson BDC all issue 'Schedules Earnings Release and Conference Call' wires). The clock does not silently run out; it is resolved by an affirmative press release that hits every terminal simultaneously. Worse, TPVG DECOUPLES the distribution from earnings and declares it a quarter FORWARD — it declared the Q4 2025 distribution ($0.23 + $0.02 supplemental) in a standalone release on 14 October 2025, i.e. BEFORE the Q3 earnings release. A declaration that precedes the disclosure cannot be 'delaying the release of bad news'; the causal channel Onali proposes is structurally absent in the specific instrument being traded. And Wall Street Horizon sells a streaming feed of dividend announcement date-times for ~5,300 companies delivered 'in sub-second time after press releases are issued on wire services', explicitly flagging dividends 'pending board approval' and those with 'base and variable components'. You are not ahead of the tape. You are behind a commercial sub-second feed, arriving with a manual screen.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: No. This is not a probabilistic objection, it is a factual refutation. The proponent asserted an empirical property of the information environment (no wire event resolves the signal) and that property does not hold for the named universe. The advance-notice wire and the forward standalone declaration are verifiable on TPVG's own IR feed. The only surviving version of the claim would be a name that neither pre-announces its earnings date nor pre-declares distributions — that must be demonstrated name-by-name before the claim can be restated, and the flagship name fails it.

kill_shots.attack: THE SELECTION SCREEN IS THE ACQUIRER'S SCREEN — the signal fires preferentially during merger negotiations, which is the worst possible state for a short. This is the confound that inverts the mechanism, and the proponent's own second representative name is the proof. MRCC announced a merger with Horizon Technology Finance (HRZN) in Q2 2025, closing Q1 2026. Dechert's BDC consolidation analysis states the acquirer's rationale explicitly: 'For a target BDC trading below its NAV, a potential acquiror may believe that an offer above the target's then current trading price but below NAV offers the target stockholders value.' Read that against the strategy's entry filter — deep discount to NAV (TPVG at 0.62x), sub-1x dividend coverage, distress. That is not merely correlated with the acquirer's screen; it IS the acquirer's screen. Now compound it: a board in live merger negotiation has every reason to defer a routine distribution declaration — deal terms are unsettled, disclosure counsel is constraining announcements, and the distribution policy is itself a negotiated term. So the 'clock slip' is generated at elevated rate precisely when a deal is being papered. The signal is POSITIVELY correlated with takeover risk, not independent of it. MRCC did both: it cut 64% AND it merged. On a 10-trade-per-year book, a single 40% deal pop costs 4.0 percentage points of average trade return — 2.6 years of the claimed gross alpha, erased by one event that the strategy actively selects for.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: No, and this is the finding I would refuse to trade around. It cannot be diversified away because it is not idiosyncratic — it is induced by the entry criterion. It cannot be stopped out, because deal announcements gap overnight. It cannot be hedged cheaply, because the options on these names are exactly where the hedge is most expensive. Screening out names already in announced deals does not help: the exposure is to UNANNOUNCED deals, and the delay signal is a leading indicator of them. The only mitigation is to abandon the distress/discount filter — which deletes the strategy.

kill_shots.attack: THE EDGE IS UNFALSIFIABLE WITHIN A HUMAN CAREER. Using the proponent's own generous parameters (p(cut)=0.20, conditional -15%, loser mixture averaging ~-1.5%), per-trade standard deviation is ~7.6% against a gross mean of ~1.5-1.8%. Reaching t=2 on the GROSS edge requires ~101 trades — 10.1 years at 10 events/yr, 33.7 years at 3 events/yr. Reaching t=2 on the best-case NET edge (+0.3%) requires ~2,593 trades — 259 to 864 years. The event count itself is admitted as ESTIMATED, never measured; no base rate was constructed. And the ~250-name screening universe means multiple-comparison inflation is entirely unaccounted for. You could trade this for a full career, lose money the whole time, and never be able to reject the hypothesis that it works. That is the definition of a strategy that cannot be risk-managed: no stopping rule is possible because no amount of losses constitutes evidence.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: Partially — but the rebuttal is a research programme, not an argument, and it must complete BEFORE any capital moves. Inter-announcement intervals are reconstructable from EDGAR 8-K Item 8.01 acceptance timestamps joined to declaration text, back to ~2004, across the full BDC/mREIT universe. That yields a real base rate, a real conditional-move distribution, and a real event count. Note this is cheap and the proponent did not do it — the review was concluded on estimates when the primary source was free and public. That omission is itself a signal about the diligence behind the other numbers.

kill_shots.attack: THE SIGNAL IS SATURATED FROM SUB-SECOND INSTITUTIONAL FEEDS DOWN TO FREE BLOG POSTS — the 'nobody is doing this' premise is false at every tier of the market simultaneously. Institutional: Wall Street Horizon's DateBreaks 3.0 is a time-stamped alert product built to identify 'companies that have not yet confirmed an earnings date and are materially late compared to their historical trends/behaviors' — that is a verbatim description of the proposed signal, productized, with a DateBreaks Factor where negative = later than historical average. WSH also runs the LERI (Late Earnings Report Index) as a published market-wide indicator, covers 11,000+ companies and 40+ event types, and distributes via FactSet, TMX and Interactive Brokers by FTP, API and streaming XML. Quantified: the RavenPack/WSH study reports a long-short strategy on this exact signal earning 19.7% annualized in Small-Caps on a 1-day window — the effect is real, published, and already packaged as a marketed factor. Retail: Simply Safe Dividends advertises '97% of dividend cuts caught in advance'; BDC Buzz sells BDC-specific coverage analysis; free sites publish 'BDC Dividend Cuts 2026: Coverage Ratio Falls Below 1x'. The proponent's own case concedes the fundamentals are 'corroborated' — i.e. public. There is no tier of this market where the information is scarce.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: No. The RavenPack 19.7% figure is the cruelest evidence available, because it looks supportive and is not: it describes a DIVERSIFIED long-short small-cap portfolio with a 1-day horizon, harvested via a sub-second machine-readable feed. The proposal is a concentrated naked short book of 3-10 names per year held three weeks, sourced manually. Same signal, opposite implementation, and the implementation is where all the money is. The published result does not validate the trade; it establishes that the trade's edge has already been captured in a form the proponent cannot compete with.

kill_shots.attack: THE CONDITIONAL MOVE IS ROUGHLY HALF WHAT IS ASSUMED, AND THAT ALONE TAKES GROSS EXPECTANCY BELOW THE FRICTION FLOOR. The proponent assumes -15% conditional, calling it 'already generous given pre-pricing'. The realized cut-day move on the proponent's own flagship name was -7%: TPVG fell 7% to a 52-week low on its Q2 2024 25% cut to $0.30. Substitute the observed number into the proponent's own arithmetic: 0.20 x 7% = +1.4% gross on winners, minus 0.80 x 1.5% = -1.2% on losers, for GROSS expectancy of +0.2% per trade — against an admitted equity-short friction floor of 1.5-3.5%. The strategy is dead at the proponent's own probability, using the proponent's own name's realized move, before borrow, before impact, before a single adverse event. And -7% overstates the dividend-attributable component, because the cut was bundled with 'worse-than-expected second quarter results' — the move is jointly caused by an NII/NAV miss you did not predict and cannot separate. MRCC is worse: its 64% cut arrived alongside a merger close and a fully telegraphed NII collapse ($0.08 NII against a $0.25 dividend, spillover exhausted) that was visible in public 10-Q data for four consecutive quarters. Separately, the friction estimates were never observed at all — MarketChameleon was behind a login wall, admitted in the brief — and the pricing is stale: TPVG was quoted at $5.41 but traded $4.57 in July 2026, ~15% lower.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: No for the equity expression, and the options expression is worse than expensive — it is structurally impossible. A $4.57 stock carries $2.50-wide strikes. A 7% move is $0.32. The move does not travel far enough to cross a strike, so the payoff never enters the region where the option pays, regardless of premium. A 20-50% premium haircut is the second problem, not the first.

kill_shots.attack: CAPACITY-DEAD IN ABSOLUTE DOLLARS, AND THE UNIVERSE IS PHYSICALLY SHRINKING. Grant every generous assumption the proponent makes — the full +1.8% gross, 10 events per year, $250k per position (the size above which impact is admitted to degrade materially). That is $45,000 per year of GROSS return, before borrow (10-40% annualized on exactly the hard-to-borrow distressed names the screen selects), before impact, before the analyst's time. Set against that: an unbounded left tail from consolidation bids and squeezes in sub-$250M-cap names. Meanwhile the tradeable universe is contracting — MRCC, one of the two named representative tickers, ceased to exist as an independent short during the period under review, absorbed into HRZN. The BDC consolidation cycle (OBDC/OBDE Jan 2025, MFIC/AFT/AIF Jul 2024, MRCC/HRZN Q1 2026) is systematically removing the subscale distressed names that constitute the entire opportunity set. The strategy's universe is being acquired out from under it, at premiums, by the same mechanism that generates its largest losses.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: No meaningful rebuttal, though the proponent already conceded capacity. The point worth adding is that capacity is not merely small — it is small AND asymmetric AND shrinking. A strategy whose maximum annual gross is ~$45k while carrying single-event downside of 40%+ on a concentrated short book is not a small-edge strategy, it is a negative-convexity lottery ticket sold at a positive price. The correct response to 'capacity is tiny' is not 'so trade it small', it is 'so the expected value of the research time exceeds the expected value of the trade'.

redteam.survives:
Almost nothing survives, and what does survive is not tradeable by this proposal.

WHAT IS GENUINELY TRUE: (1) The underlying academic relationship is real — Onali (2016), Economics Letters 146, pp. 71-76 is correctly cited by the reviewer, who also correctly caught the brainstorm's misattribution to Journal of Corporate Finance. (2) The effect replicates commercially — the RavenPack/Wall Street Horizon study reports 19.7% annualized in small-caps. (3) The BDC sector stress is real and corroborated: median coverage 0.99x, 0.89x ex-PIK, with genuine cuts landing.

WHY NONE OF THAT HELPS: The proponent's honest self-assessment (net negative to break-even, decisively negative for options) is CORRECT IN DIRECTION BUT NOT SEVERE ENOUGH, because it rests on three inputs that the evidence contradicts. Substituting observed values for assumed ones moves the verdict from marginal to decisive:

- Conditional move: assumed -15%, observed -7% on the flagship name. This alone drops gross expectancy from +1.8% to +0.2%, i.e. below the friction floor. The strategy fails on the proponent's own arithmetic with one input corrected.
- Latency edge: assumed structural, actually nonexistent. TPVG pre-announces its earnings date by wire ~2 weeks ahead AND pre-declares distributions a quarter forward in standalone releases. There is no absence to infer from, and a declaration that precedes disclosure cannot be delaying bad news.
- Independence of the entry filter: assumed, actually inverted. The screen selects for takeover targets, and delayed declarations cluster in live merger negotiations.

THE STRUCTURAL ERROR, which is worth more than any individual finding: the strategy conflates PREDICTING A CUT with PREDICTING A RETURN. Onali's paper predicts cuts. It contains no abnormal-return study. In a cohort trading at 0.62x NAV on a 17% yield with sub-1x coverage published freely by multiple vendors and by free websites, p(cut) is both high and universally known — which is precisely why the yield is 17%. A high, correctly-anticipated probability of a cut generates no return when it resolves. The proponent's own framing concedes this ('already generous given pre-pricing') and then declines to follow it to the conclusion. There is also genuine SIGN uncertainty, not merely magnitude uncertainty: a cut that arrests NAV erosion is routinely read as right-sizing, and sector commentary explicitly distinguishes rate-driven cuts (PFLT) from credit-driven ones. You can be right about the cut and still lose.

Two secondary problems finish it. The signal is not measurable in this cohort: Onali measured intervals between clean quarterly regular dividends of 1971-2014 industrials, but modern BDCs pay base + supplemental + special on irregular cadence (CCAP declared a Q3 base plus three extra 2026 installments in a single release; TPVG declared $0.23 base + $0.02 supplemental). Defining 'the interval between dividend announcements' in that structure requires arbitrary choices that are pure researcher degrees of freedom — and with 3-10 events per year, those choices determine the backtest result entirely. And the declaration cadence is driven by RIC mechanics — the ~90% distribution requirement, spillover balances, excise-tax year-end management, board calendars — none of which is news suppression.

VERDICT: DO NOT TRADE. Not 'trade smaller', not 'trade it as a long-only tilt'. The equity expression is negative-expectancy with a takeover tail the entry filter actively recruits. The options expression is impossible, not merely expensive — a 7% move on a $4.57 stock with $2.50-wide strikes never reaches the payoff region. The one intellectually honest use of this work is as a negative result: the reviewer's own caveats were well-calibrated and the correct action is to bank the discipline and kill the idea.

The most damning single fact: during the review period, one of the two named representative tickers was acquired. The strategy's universe is being bought out at premiums by the same force that constitutes its largest loss scenario.
redteam.required_evidence:
For this to work, ALL of the following must be true simultaneously. Each is individually testable, several are cheap, and at least three are already known to be FALSE.

1. [KNOWN FALSE] There exists a meaningful set of names that pre-announce NEITHER their earnings date NOR their distribution. TPVG does both. Test: pull every 8-K Item 7.01/8.01 for the candidate universe and measure advance notice on scheduling releases. Kills the latency claim if median notice > 0 days, which it demonstrably is.

2. [KNOWN FALSE] The signal is not already commercialized. Wall Street Horizon DateBreaks 3.0 flags 'not yet confirmed and materially late vs. historical trend' and streams dividend announcements sub-second to FactSet/TMX/IBKR subscribers.

3. [KNOWN FALSE, ~-7% vs -15% assumed] Conditional single-session move on a genuine surprise cut is at least -12%, measured cleanly, EXCLUDING cuts bundled with earnings misses or merger news. Test: event study on every BDC/mREIT cut 2015-2026, decomposing the move against same-day NII/NAV surprise. If the dividend-attributable residual is under ~-10%, the trade cannot clear frictions at any plausible p.

4. [UNTESTED, AND THE DECIDING TEST] Delayed declarations are NOT predictive of merger announcements. This is the inverting confound and the single most important thing to measure. Test: hazard model of P(merger announced within 90 days | declaration interval in top decile) across the BDC universe 2010-2026. If the hazard is elevated at all, the strategy is short a takeover-target factor and must be abandoned regardless of how every other test resolves.

5. [UNTESTED] A base rate exists at all. Reconstruct inter-announcement intervals from EDGAR 8-K acceptance timestamps back to ~2004 and produce a MEASURED event count and P(cut | tight flag). The claimed 3-10/yr and p=0.20 are currently unsourced estimates. Free, public, and not done.

6. [UNTESTED, PROBABLY UNRESOLVABLE] The interval is definable without researcher discretion in a base+supplemental+special regime. Pre-register the definition, then show results are stable across every reasonable alternative. With 3-10 events/yr, if the answer moves under definitional perturbation, there is no finding.

7. [UNTESTED] The conditional move is reliably NEGATIVE in sign for deep-discount names, i.e. no systematic relief rally when a cut preserves NAV. Test: split realized cut reactions by P/NAV and by coverage ratio at announcement. If names below ~0.7x NAV show non-negative mean reaction, the trade is backwards in exactly the cohort it targets.

8. [UNTESTED] Observed — not estimated — borrow, spread and impact on the live candidate list, sized to intended capital. The brief's figures came from a login wall and stale prices ($5.41 quoted vs $4.57 traded). Get a real locate quote and a real Level 2 book before any number in the friction section is believed.

9. [ARITHMETICALLY FALSE AT ANY REALISTIC HORIZON] Statistical power sufficient to distinguish the edge from zero within the capital's lifetime. Gross needs ~101 trades (10-34 yrs); net needs ~2,593 (259-864 yrs). Unless events are far more frequent than estimated, no live-trading evidence can ever confirm or refute this. Absent a pre-registered historical test that clears 1-8, running it live is not an experiment — it is an unmonitorable bet.

PRIORITY: run test 4 first. It is the cheapest decisive one, and if the merger hazard is elevated the remaining tests are moot.

redteam.target: Call Report Amendment Autopsy — short microcap/community banks (hedged with KRE) within days of an adverse FFIEC Call Report amendment, holding 1-6 weeks into the 10-Q. VERDICT: KILL. Not a close call. The proponent reached the right conclusion via a partly wrong statistic and missed the two facts in their own cited source that break the causal chain outright. Every one of the six attack axes lands; four are independently fatal, and the friction/capacity kill and the mechanism kill are in direct logical contradiction with each other's escape hatches, so no filter rescues it.

kill_shots.attack: MECHANISM INVERSION — the amendment arrives AFTER the 10-Q, not before. The stated mechanism is that the versioned diff 'front-runs the documents analysts actually read... holding 1-6 weeks into the bank's 10-Q.' BBE Table 2 Panel A gives days between original and restated Call Report: mean 22.18, median 19, Q1 11, Q3 33. Originals cluster at day 30 (56% on day 30; 92% on days 27-31). So amendments land at roughly day 41 (Q1), day 49 (median), day 63 (Q3). The 10-Q deadline is 40 days for accelerated filers and 45 days for non-accelerated. At least half — and by Q3, three quarters — of amendments arrive after the 10-Q is already public. You are not front-running the document analysts read; you are trading a stale correction to a report the market has already superseded twice (earnings release, then 10-Q). The trade is arithmetically backwards for the majority of the sample.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: Only by filtering to amendments arriving before day 40-45. That retains <25% of an already collapsed sample, driving tradeable events below 1/year and making the frequency and power kills strictly worse. The escape hatch feeds the next kill.

kill_shots.attack: NO ECONOMIC CONTENT — the payload is empty, per the proponent's own source. Of 970 amendments, only 114 (11.8%) changed total assets at all: mean $2.95M = 0.158% of assets, MEDIAN 0.042%. Only 198 (20.4%) changed Tier 1 at all: mean 0.210pp, median 0.060pp, Q3 0.210pp — BBE describe this as a 1.3% (mean) / 0.4% (median) change in the Tier 1 ratio. A 6-basis-point median revision to a regulatory capital ratio is not information about anything. BBE's own conclusion: amendments 'tend to be immaterial as evidenced by the small mean size of the errors and the lack of market reaction.' The strategy requires a quasi-restatement; the data shows a rounding correction.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: No. The only opening is that the tail (>1pp Tier 1 revision) is real — but see the frequency kill: fitting the reported mean/sd puts that tail at ~4.6 events/year across the ENTIRE listed universe, ~1 in the microcap tail. The tail exists and is empty of trade count.

kill_shots.attack: WRONG CAUSAL AGENT — the modal amendment is FDIC clerical hygiene, not a management confession. BBE: 'amendments are particularly common in the first 16 days after release; the first 16 days account for 46 percent of the total amendments,' and an FDIC staff member explained these 'likely stem from detailed reviews of the Call Reports conducted by FDIC analysts during the two weeks following submission.' Nearly half of all amendments are a regulator's desk analyst flagging a classification or validation issue and the bank refiling. FFIEC policy separately permits revision 'without prejudice' within 30 days of the filing deadline — amendments in that window are explicitly sanctioned routine. The signal generator is not 'bank discovers credit deterioration'; it is 'FDIC reviewer caught a mislabeled line.' The causal chain the trade depends on is severed at the source.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: Partial and weak. BBE do note regulators told them more significant errors should be corrected via amendment while less significant ones go through a cumulative-effect adjustment on schedule RI-A line 2 — so amendments are the higher-severity channel by design. This is the single fact that cuts for the proponent. It fails anyway because the realized magnitudes on that supposedly-higher-severity channel are still 6bp of Tier 1.

kill_shots.attack: UNFALSIFIABLE BY CONSTRUCTION — you can neither backtest it nor live-validate it within a working life. Double bind. (a) No backtest is possible: amendments overwrite history (BBE: 'SNL Financial overwrites its record of the original filing when there is an amendment'), FFIEC PDD serves the current vintage, and the available historical panels — Chicago Fed commercial bank data 1976-2021, WRDS Bank Regulatory — are as-revised panels, not point-in-time vintages. The archive must be accumulated forward. (b) Forward validation is unreachable: at ~1.1 tradeable events/year with 4-week KRE-hedged idiosyncratic vol of 10.6-14.1%, detecting even a generous +5% edge at t=2 requires n=18-32 events = 16-28 years; a realistic +2% edge requires n=113-200 events = 99-175 years. So capital gets deployed for decades on a signal that can never be confirmed, while the only sample that exists carries a negative point estimate. This is the true kill: not that the edge is proven negative, but that the design makes 'proven' structurally unreachable while the costs are paid up front.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: No. And note this attack is immune to the proponent's own strongest defense — that BBE tested only the 2-day window, not the 1-6 week drift. Even granting the drift hypothesis is untested, the drift hypothesis is precisely the thing that needs 99-175 years to test.

kill_shots.attack: CAPACITY-DEAD — the strategy cannot pay for its own server. Verified independently: MBBC ~$41.6M cap, $14.06, ~1.32K shares/day = ~$18K/day of total dollar volume. At a disciplined 10%-of-ADV participation, a 20-trading-day build caps the position at ~$33K in MBBC, ~$62K in CPBI — and the build consumes the entire 1-6 week holding period, so you finish entering as you should be exiting. Combined with ~1-2 genuine events/year, total annual gross exposure is roughly $70K. Run the P&L: at a fantasy 10% gross edge against a charitable 4% round-trip friction, that is $4,200/year. At a realistic 3% gross against 10% friction it is -$4,900/year. There is no position size at which this covers the maintenance of the ingestion pipeline, let alone labor or the cost of capital.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: Only by moving up-cap to the liquid tail where friction falls to 0.4-1.2%. But the entire 'why under-exploited' premise is that the edge lives in the $200M-$2B banks with zero analyst coverage. Moving to where you can trade moves to where the claimed inefficiency does not exist. This is a direct contradiction, not a tradeoff.

kill_shots.attack: FREQUENCY COLLAPSE — ~1-2 tradeable events/year, roughly an order of magnitude below the claimed 15-25. Rebuilding the funnel from BBE primitives rather than the proponent's summary: ~726 amendments/yr across ~500 listed banks; 20.4% move Tier 1 at all = 148/yr; fitting a lognormal to (mean 0.210pp, sd 0.414pp) puts only ~3.1% above a 1.0pp revision = 4.6/yr materially moving capital across the whole listed universe; ~50% in the $200M-$2B tail = 2.3/yr; ~50% adverse and therefore shortable = ~1.1/yr. One trade per year. Any strategy at that event rate is indistinguishable from a discretionary hunch and cannot support a systematic pipeline.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: Marginal. Smaller banks likely amend at a higher rate than BBE's sample (median assets $2.1B, mean $44.5B — the target cohort sits at or below the bottom of it). But higher amendment rates among less-sophisticated filers implies MORE clerical noise, not more signal. The extrapolation that raises the count also degrades the average quality.

kill_shots.attack: ADVERSE-SELECTION ON THE SHORT LEG — you are systematically short a takeover call option in the exact cohort where the option is live. Micro community bank stocks trade below 0.9x tangible book; median M&A pricing is ~150% of tangible common equity with an average ~30% takeover premium, and 37% of surveyed banks report having been approached in 2024-25 in an actively reopening deal market. Worse, the named targets (MBBC, CPBI, FSEA, NSTS, TCBS, CLST) are recent mutual-holding-company/thrift conversions — a cohort whose price is driven by second-step conversion speculation, buybacks, and takeout odds, NOT by asset quality. The signal is orthogonal to the dominant price driver. At ~1-2 trades/year, a single deal announcement during a 1-6 week hold erases a decade of the hypothesized edge.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: No practical one. The natural fix — buy puts instead of shorting to cap the tail — is unavailable (see execution kill). The KRE hedge does not help: it hedges sector beta, while the risk is a single-name idiosyncratic bid.

kill_shots.attack: EXECUTION IMPOSSIBLE — no options exist, and the short leg may not be borrowable. Listed options require float and volume thresholds these names miss by orders of magnitude (Nasdaq/Cboe minimum ~$15M public float plus volume tests; standard options-listing criteria run to ~7M publicly held shares and ~2.4M shares ADV). MBBC at ~1,179-1,320 shares/day is three orders of magnitude short. So 'buy put spreads' — the defined-risk fallback written into the idea spec — simply does not exist in the target universe. That leaves borrowing and shorting a name with ~$17-31K/day of total dollar volume, where a locate is unlikely, the fee is punitive if found, and a recall at the wrong moment is a forced buy-in into a market you are 1.6-3.0x larger than.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: No. This is a hard structural constraint, not a cost to be optimized. It also removes the only mechanism that would have bounded the takeover-pop tail risk.

kill_shots.attack: NO MOAT — the collection layer is commoditized and a vendor already tracks amendments. The claimed edge is that 'nobody treats it as a versioned document stream.' The tooling is a pip install: ffiec-data-connect wraps all 7 FFIEC REST endpoints at 2,500 req/hr, plus call-report/data-collector, chosak/fdic-call-reports, henryroyal/ffiec, acurley/ffiec, and ketchbrookanalytics/ffiec are all public. BankRegData/BankRegReports states it syncs new FFIEC and NCUA filings each reporting season 'including late amendments.' The barrier to entry is an afternoon.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: Yes, partially, and this is the proponent's fairest point. The TOOLS are commoditized but the ARCHIVE is not — a point-in-time vintage panel cannot be bought or reconstructed after the fact, only accumulated forward, and nobody appears to publish one. The moat is genuine. It just guards an empty vault: a real, scarce, defensible dataset about an event with 6bp of median economic content and one tradeable instance per year.

kill_shots.attack: NON-REPORTING TARGETS — for much of the target cohort there is no 10-Q to cash the signal into. JOBS Act §601 (2012) raised the bank/BHC deregistration threshold from 300 to 1,200 holders of record (registration trigger 2,000); roughly 500 community banks deregistered. For any deregistered target there is no 10-Q, no 8-K, and no proxy — so the strategy's stated exit catalyst ('holding 1-6 weeks into the bank's 10-Q or next earnings release') does not exist, and the stock sits on OTC venues with liquidity worse than the already-untradeable Nasdaq names cited. The named targets are recent conversions and do still file, but the broader $200M-$2B universe the funnel count depends on is materially non-reporting.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: Yes — restrict to SEC registrants. But this shrinks the universe again, compounding the frequency kill, and it selects for exactly the recent-conversion cohort most exposed to the takeover-pop tail.

kill_shots.attack: THE PROPONENT'S HEADLINE STATISTIC IS MISREAD (a correction, not a rescue). BBE's RET and VOL are MAGNITUDE metrics — abnormal absolute price movement and volume ratios, non-event mean RET = 1.171 — not signed returns. 'RET difference -0.0122' is therefore not a -1.22% return, and 'measured gross edge on the exact event is 0.00%' misdescribes what was measured. Correctly stated the result is worse for the strategy: on the 758 clean amendments the market shows no abnormal absolute price movement and no abnormal volume — it does not twitch. A directional trade needs dispersion to harvest and there is none on the event.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: This cuts both ways and I state it honestly: because BBE measured only the two-day (0,+1) window, the paper does NOT test the 1-6 week drift the strategy actually claims. That is the proponent's single strongest available counter and their 'statistical kill' is partly misapplied. It rescues nothing — the drift hypothesis is unfalsifiable on a 99-175 year horizon and there is 6bp of content to drift on — but the case should be argued correctly.

kill_shots.attack: THE INFORMATIONAL LEAD IS REAL — and this is the axis where the attack FAILS. I could not break claims (1) through (5). RetrieveFilersSubmissionDateTime does exist as a REST endpoint (ffieccdr.azure-api.us/public/RetrieveFilersSubmissionDateTime) returning RSSD IDs and submission datetimes for filers since a given timestamp — a genuine, cheap amendment detector at 2,500 req/hr. Amendments genuinely do erase history and are genuinely not reconstructable. There is genuinely no 8-K, no press release, and no newswire on an amendment. For the ~25% of amendments that precede the 10-Q there is a real, exclusive informational lead over every other public document. The asymmetry is authentic. It is simply an exclusive lead on a fact that does not matter — which is the worst kind of edge, because it is seductive, verifiable, and worthless.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: N/A — this attack does not land. Conceding it is important: the failure here is not informational, it is economic and statistical. Do not let the reality of the data asymmetry be mistaken for evidence of tradeable content.

redteam.survives:
TWO THINGS SURVIVE, NEITHER OF WHICH IS THE PROPOSED TRADE.

1) THE DATASET, AS AN ASSET — NOT AS A SIGNAL. A forward-collected, point-in-time vintage archive of Call Report filings is genuinely scarce, genuinely cheap (free registration, ~2,500 req/hr, one endpoint), and genuinely impossible to reconstruct after the fact — no vendor or academic panel publishes as-filed vintages, only as-revised ones. Build it as infrastructure and let it accrue. Its value is optionality on future applications, and it costs nearly nothing to run. Do not attach capital to its output.

2) THE PIVOT THE PROPOSAL WALKED PAST — TRADE THE ORIGINAL FILING, NOT THE AMENDMENT. The same paper used to kill the amendment trade contains a live, measured, universe-wide result the proposal ignored: original Call Reports DO move stocks. 'Mean price volatility (trading volume) around Call Report release dates is 8.4 percent (8.6 percent) higher than the non-event day mean,' statistically significant, and concentrated entirely in CALL2 (Call Report released AFTER the earnings announcement); CALL1 shows volume but no price reaction, and Y-9Cs and 10-K/Qs show nothing. Early Call Reports even preempt earnings — the EA2 coefficient is 40% lower in the RET regression. Release timing is highly predictable: 56% on day 30, 92% across days 27-31. That is a dated, repeating, ~2,000-events-per-year phenomenon versus ~1 per year for material amendments — roughly three orders of magnitude more testable, and it can be studied on existing as-revised panels because the original day-30 filing is the event.

Critically, the RI-E free-text leg of the idea belongs to THIS trade, not the amendment trade: the RI-E itemization of the three largest 'other noninterest expense' components is filed WITH the original report at day 30. A first-appearance 'litigation settlement' string is a day-30 original-filing signal that has been misfiled under 'amendment' in the proposal. That is the salvageable hypothesis.

WHAT MUST BE TRUE FOR THE AMENDMENT TRADE ITSELF — six conditions, at least two pairs of which are mutually contradictory:
(1) A sub-class of amendments with >1pp Tier 1 revision must occur far more than ~5x/yr universe-wide, contradicting the fitted BBE magnitude distribution.
(2) That sub-class must be separable ex ante from the ~46% FDIC-desk-review clerical amendments using the diff alone — with no labelled training data in existence.
(3) The amendment must arrive before day 40-45, true for <25% of amendments.
(4) A 1-6 week drift of >=5% must be real despite a zero two-day reaction and a 6bp median Tier 1 revision.
(5) It must execute in names liquid enough to matter — but the claimed inefficiency exists only where liquidity does not.
(6) No takeover bid may arrive during any hold, in a sub-book-value cohort inside an active M&A cycle, with no listed puts available to cap that tail.
