Conditions (3) and (5) directly contradict (1) and (4): every filter that makes the signal cleaner makes the sample smaller and the universe less tradeable. The failure is overdetermined — it is not one broken assumption but a structure in which fixing any one break widens another.

RECOMMENDATION: Do not allocate. Build the vintage archive as a cheap standing dataset, redirect the research effort to the day-30 original-filing event and the RI-E text screen in names that clear a $2M/day dollar-volume floor, and revisit amendments only if the archive itself later shows a magnitude distribution that contradicts BBE.
redteam.required_evidence:
To reopen the amendment trade, ALL of the following would be required before any capital is committed — and note the first item alone costs 3-5 years:

1. FORWARD-COLLECTED PANEL: >=200 amendments in the $200M-$2B listed cohort with signed, size-classified diffs, collected point-in-time. No backtest substitute exists — the history is destroyed by construction. At observed rates this is 3-5 years of pure collection with zero trading.

2. MAGNITUDE DISTRIBUTION CONTRADICTING BBE: direct evidence that amendments revising Tier 1 by >1pp occur >=10x/year among listed banks. The fitted distribution (mean 0.210pp, sd 0.414pp) says ~4.6/year universe-wide. If the microcap tail genuinely amends larger, that must be shown in collected data, not assumed by extrapolation from a sample whose median bank ($2.1B assets) sits at the TOP of the target range.

3. PRE-REGISTERED ADVERSE TAXONOMY: a benign-vs-adverse classifier specified in advance, with out-of-sample hit rate, that demonstrably separates FDIC-desk-review corrections (46% of amendments, concentrated in the first 16 days post-release) from genuine credit or capital revisions. Frozen before any return is examined.

4. TIMING PROOF: demonstration that the amendment precedes the 10-Q in the tested subset — i.e. lands before day 40 (accelerated) / day 45 (non-accelerated). Any event failing this is disqualified, and the surviving count must be reported.

5. DRIFT EVIDENCE WITH REAL POWER: KRE-hedged residual returns over the 1-6 week horizon with t>2 on n>=100 events. Anything less is unfalsifiable noise. Given ~1-2 qualifying events/year this is the binding constraint and is likely unreachable — which is itself the answer.

6. LIVE EXECUTION EVIDENCE, NOT QUOTED SPREADS: actual borrow locates obtained and actual fills on >=10 attempted entries, proving realized round-trip cost <2% and confirming that a position can be built in less time than the holding period. Quoted spreads and ADV-based estimates are inadmissible in this universe — a $50k order is 1.6-3.0x total daily dollar volume in the named targets.

7. TAIL-RISK PLAN: a stated, funded answer to the takeover-pop scenario in a cohort trading below tangible book with median deals at ~150% of TCE and ~30% premiums, given that listed puts do not exist on these names.

STOPPING RULE: if items 2, 4, or 6 fail — and current evidence says all three do — the strategy is dead regardless of what items 1, 3, 5 and 7 show.

playbooks.name: Day-30 Call Report Delta (liquid bank cross-section)
playbooks.verdict: FORWARD TEST ONLY — ZERO CAPITAL until Test 1 clears its pre-registered criterion. This is the sole survivor of 40, and it is not one of the 40 as proposed: it is the salvage the Call Report red team carved out while killing the amendment trade. It inherits none of the amendment trade's fatal features — it trades the ORIGINAL day-30 filing (not the amendment), in the $2M+/day liquid tail (not $17k/day microcaps), at ~480 events/year (not 1-3), and it is backtestable on free existing panels (not accumulate-forward). Prior that it clears the go/no-go: roughly 25-35%. Even if it clears, expect a modest, capacity-limited sleeve — Sharpe 0.4-0.7, low-single-digit percent annual net on the sleeve — not a franchise. It earns one to two weeks of an analyst's time because the test is cheap and DECISIVE, which is the exact property every other idea in the catalog lacked.
playbooks.universe: US exchange-listed bank holding companies whose lead depository files an FFIEC 031/041/051 Call Report, filtered to: 60-day median dollar volume >= $2,000,000/day, price >= $5, US primary listing, and a clean ticker->BHC->lead-bank RSSD mapping. That is roughly 130-180 names (approximately the KRE constituent set plus the remaining $500M+ cap listed banks) out of the ~428-600 listed bank universe. HARD EXCLUSIONS, and these are the point of the pivot, not incidental: no name below $2M/day; no recent mutual-holding-company or thrift conversion (MBBC, CPBI, FSEA, CLST, TCBS, NSTS, KFFB and cohort — the entire target universe of the killed amendment trade); no OTC/deregistered bank; no name with borrow > 3% annualized on the short leg. Event filter: only CALL2 bank-quarters, i.e. those where the Call Report submission timestamp is AFTER the earnings-announcement timestamp. Per BBE the price reaction lives entirely in CALL2; CALL1 shows volume without price response. EA precedes the Call Report in ~81% of bank-quarters, so this retains ~480 events/year across the tradeable universe.
playbooks.signal: PRE-REGISTERED cross-sectional composite of quarter-over-quarter deltas drawn ONLY from schedules that are not in a typical bank earnings release. Core (highest prior on freshness): (a) Schedule RC-N — change in 30-89 days past due, by loan category (CRE non-owner-occupied, construction & development, multifamily, C&I), scaled to loans; 30-89 DPD is essentially never disclosed in a bank press release and it leads NPAs by 1-2 quarters. (b) Schedule RI-B — net charge-offs by category and the ALLL rebuild ratio (provision less NCO, scaled to loans). (c) Schedule RC-C — change in construction and total-CRE concentration as a percent of total risk-based capital, relative to the 100%/300% supervisory guidance thresholds. Secondary/control (KNOWN CROWDED since 2023, include as a control regressor, do NOT let it drive the composite): Schedule RC-O uninsured and brokered deposits. Separate leg B: Schedule RI-E memoranda itemizing the components of 'Other noninterest expense' exceeding 10% of that line, with their free-text descriptors — flag FIRST-APPEARANCE strings matching a fixed lexicon (litigation, settlement, fraud, restitution, consent order, impairment, severance). Verify current MDRM codes against the live FFIEC 031/041/051 instructions before building; the schedules were renumbered in the 2024-25 Call Report modernization. COMPOSITE: winsorize each input at 1/99, z-score within the quarter's cross-section, sign-orient so positive = deteriorating, equal-weight. Weights and inputs frozen in a signed file BEFORE any return is examined. DATA ENDPOINTS AND CADENCE: (1) FFIEC CDR Public Data Distribution web service, https://cdr.ffiec.gov/public/pws/webservices/retrievalservice.asmx (spec CDR-PDD-SIS-611 v1.10) and the REST mirror ffieccdr.azure-api.us — free registration, Entra ID JWT, 90-day token with NO refresh (put a hard calendar reminder on day 80; unattended-job token expiry is the known operational failure mode). Rate limit ~2,500 req/hr. Poll RetrieveFilersSubmissionDateTime daily at 07:00 ET across days 25-45 after quarter-end to detect new filings (56% land on day 30, 92% across days 27-31), then RetrieveFacsimile for the schedules. (2) SEC EDGAR daily index / 8-K Item 2.02 acceptance timestamps for the earnings-announcement date that determines CALL1 vs CALL2. (3) FFIEC NIC + FDIC BankFind for the RSSD->BHC->ticker crosswalk, rebuilt quarterly. (4) Any daily OHLCV source for the liquidity screen. Total marginal data cost: $0.
playbooks.entry: Only for CALL2 bank-quarters. On detection of a new original filing, compute the composite against the quarter's cross-section as it accumulates; freeze ranks at 17:00 ET on day 32 after quarter-end (by which ~92% of filings are in). Enter the following session between 10:00 and 10:30 ET. Order type: marketable limit at the NBBO midpoint plus a hard 15bp cap, sliced; NEVER a market order. If a name is not filled at the 15bp cap within 30 minutes, DROP IT and do not chase — a name you cannot fill inside 15bp is a name where a sub-1% edge does not survive. No entries in a name with an unresolved M&A announcement, a pending capital raise, or an FDIC/OCC enforcement action disclosed in the prior 5 sessions.
playbooks.expression: Common shares only. Dollar-neutral long/short: long the 15 most-improving composite names, short the 15 most-deteriorating, equal-weighted within each leg, with residual sector exposure hedged by a KRE overlay sized to the net beta of the book (KRE spread 1-2bp, deep ADV — the one cheap piece of the killed idea that carries over). Leg B (RI-E first-appearance) enters as an additional short in the deteriorating leg only, capped at 3 names. NO OPTIONS, at any stage. Listed options on banks run 5-15% of premium round-trip and IV is bid into earnings; a signal that will at best be tens of basis points cannot pay that. If the backtest shows the edge concentrated in a handful of $10B+ names with penny-wide options, revisit then — not before.
playbooks.sizing: STAGE 0 (now): $0. Research only. STAGE 1 (only if Test 1 clears): paper-trade one full quarter, then forward-test at 1/10 of terminal size for four quarters. STAGE 2 (only if Stage 1 realized net spread is positive and within one standard error of the backtest point estimate): scale to terminal. TERMINAL LIMITS: sleeve <= 15% of book NAV; per-name <= min(0.75% of sleeve NAV, 5% of that name's 20-day ADV); minimum 12 names per side (concentration below that turns the sleeve into a stock-picking bet, and the cross-sectional breadth is the only source of statistical power here); gross <= 2.0x sleeve NAV; hard reject any short with borrow > 3% annualized — this filter, not judgment, is what keeps the book out of the hard-to-borrow adverse-selection cohort that killed the parent idea.
playbooks.exit: Unconditional 21-calendar-day hold from entry, OR the session after the name's 10-Q is filed, WHICHEVER COMES FIRST — the 10-Q supersedes the Call Report information and the edge, if any, is consumed at that point. Rebalance the whole book at each quarterly event; no carry-over positions. FORCED EXITS, no discretion: (a) any M&A announcement on either leg, same session (note the two-sided book makes the deal tail far less asymmetric than the pure-short structure that killed the amendment trade, but exit anyway); (b) borrow recall; (c) an 8-K disclosing a capital raise, enforcement action, or auditor/CFO change; (d) sleeve drawdown of 4% from its high-water mark within a single event window — flatten and stand down until the next quarter.
playbooks.costs: Per paired round trip (one long + one short + the KRE overlay share), in the $2M+/day universe: bid-ask 3-8bp round trip; market impact at a 5%-of-ADV participation cap 5-15bp; commissions ~0.5-1bp; borrow on the short leg 30-100bp annualized = 2-6bp over 21 days; KRE overlay 1-2bp. ALL-IN: approximately 20-40bp per paired round trip, call it 30bp for planning. That is the entire justification for the pivot — the killed amendment trade carried 400-1,000bp of round-trip friction in its target names. The go/no-go hurdle is set at 2.5x this friction floor deliberately.
playbooks.monitoring: (1) Rolling 8-quarter realized net decile spread versus the backtest point estimate; HALT the strategy if the rolling net spread is negative for 4 consecutive quarters. Unlike every other idea in this catalog, this stopping rule is actually reachable: ~60 name-events per side per year gives usable quarterly t-statistics, and the 16-year backtest supplies the prior to test against. (2) CALL2 SHARE — track the fraction of bank-quarters where the Call Report post-dates the earnings release. The entire effect is carried by CALL2; if banks accelerate filing ahead of earnings and that share falls below ~65%, the carrier is disappearing and the strategy should be wound down regardless of recent P&L. (3) SCHEDULE CONTINUITY — the 2024-25 Call Report modernization and the FDIC's reduced-reporting proposals can silently break field definitions; run a quarterly field-level continuity diff and freeze trading for any quarter where a core input's definition changed. (4) CROWDING — monitor BankRegData/BankRegReports, S&P Capital IQ Pro and Bloomberg for productization of 30-89 DPD deltas and RI-E text specifically; RC-O uninsured deposits is already crowded and is the template for how the rest decays. (5) Token/pipeline health: alert on JWT age > 80 days, on any day 25-45 poll returning zero new filers, and on RSSD crosswalk misses.
playbooks.first_test: TEST 1 — a retrospective event study on free existing data. This is the whole gate, and it costs one to two weeks of one analyst plus under $500. BUILD: Call Report bulk downloads (FFIEC CDR bulk / Chicago Fed commercial bank files, free, 2001-present) plus EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02 acceptance timestamps plus daily OHLCV, for listed banks 2010-2025 — roughly 150 names x 60 quarters = ~9,000 bank-quarters, of which ~7,300 are CALL2. Freeze the composite definition and weights in a signed file first. Measure the KRE-hedged (or bank-peer-neutral) mean abnormal return from t+1 to t+21, top decile minus bottom decile. SUCCESS CRITERION, stated in advance and not negotiable after the fact: decile spread >= +80bp per 21-day event with t >= 3.0 on >= 1,500 CALL2 events, AND consistent in sign across ALL THREE robustness cuts — (a) 2010-2017 versus 2018-2025 sub-samples, (b) excluding 2020Q1-Q2 and 2023Q1-Q2, (c) dropping the ~36% of bank-quarters whose Call Report was later amended, since the historical panel is as-revised not as-filed and that is the one genuine contamination in the test. PLUS a placebo: the same composite applied on a random non-filing day in the same quarter must produce < 20bp. LEG B criterion, measured in the same pass: first-appearance RI-E lexicon hits must show a mean 21-day hedged return <= -150bp on n >= 100 events. KILL RULE: if the spread is under 40bp, or |t| < 3.0, or the sign flips in any robustness cut — stop. No forward test, no capital, delete the idea. Do not re-specify the composite and re-run; that is the researcher-degrees-of-freedom failure the Dividend Clock Slip red team correctly identified as fatal.

playbook.allocation:
FUND NOTHING TODAY. Thirty-nine of forty ideas get zero dollars and zero further research time. The fortieth — Day-30 Call Report Delta — gets research time only: one to two weeks of one analyst and under $500 of data, with $0 of capital at risk. If Test 1 misses its pre-registered criterion, the correct portfolio position from this entire catalog is 100% cash, and the catalog's return is the screening discipline it produced, not P&L. That is a real and acceptable outcome; a forty-idea catalog that yields one cheap decisive experiment has done its job.

DO NOT FUND, SPECIFICALLY AND BY NAME:

1. THE AMENDMENT TRADE IN ANY FORM, INCLUDING SMALLER OR MORE FILTERED. The red team is right that the failure is overdetermined and that the escape hatches contradict each other: every filter that makes the signal cleaner (>1pp Tier 1 revision, pre-10-Q arrival) shrinks the sample toward one event per year, and every filter that makes it tradeable (liquidity, borrow, options) moves you into the cohort where the measured edge is exactly zero. There is no size at which $70k of annual gross exposure pays for an ingestion pipeline. 'Trade it smaller' is not a rescue; it is the same trade with the same sign.

2. THE DIVIDEND CLOCK SLIP IN ANY FORM — not smaller, not long-only, not as a tilt, not as a screen input. Three independently fatal facts (the date is affirmatively wired ~2 weeks ahead and streamed sub-second; the observed conditional move is roughly half the assumed one, which alone puts gross expectancy below the friction floor; and the entry filter recruits takeover targets) are unrebutted. One of its two named tickers was acquired during the review. Bank the negative result.

3. ANY MICROCAP BANK SHORT BOOK. The $40-300M cap, $17-31k/day, recent-thrift-conversion cohort (MBBC, CPBI, FSEA, CLST, TCBS, NSTS, KFFB and peers) is disqualified as a venue regardless of what signal points at it: a $50k order is 1.6-3.0x total daily dollar volume, borrow is frequently unobtainable at any price, no listed options exist so there is no defined-risk route, and you are systematically short a live takeover call in a cohort trading below tangible book with median deals at ~150% of TCE.

4. ANY OPTIONS EXPRESSION OF ANYTHING IN THIS CATALOG. Every options leg proposed across the forty was either non-existent (no listed options at the target market caps), or priced at 20-50% of premium round-trip against a signal worth a few hundred basis points, or structurally unreachable (a 7% move on a $4.57 stock with $2.50-wide strikes never enters the payoff region). The survivor's playbook forbids options at every stage.

5. ANY IDEA WHOSE CENTRAL EDGE CLAIM IS 'NO VENDOR SELLS THIS.' Some version of that claim was made in the majority of the forty and was false or irrelevant in essentially every case that got checked — Wall Street Horizon, BankRegData, Audit Analytics, dv01, Octus/9fin, Warranty Week, OPIS/Platts, Simply Safe Dividends, free public trackers. Absence of a retail product is not absence of knowledge. Treat that sentence as a red flag in future briefs, not as a thesis.

6. ANY IDEA WITH FEWER THAN ~50 TRADEABLE EVENTS PER YEAR. This is the most valuable rule the catalog produced and it kills the largest share of it. Both fully-refereed ideas died on the same arithmetic: gross-edge falsification required 101 trades (10-34 years) in one case and 18-32 events (16-28 years) in the other; net-edge falsification required centuries. A strategy that cannot be falsified within the capital's lifetime cannot be risk-managed, because no amount of losses ever constitutes evidence and no stopping rule can exist. The survivor was selected substantially BECAUSE it has ~480 events/year and a 16-year backtestable history — that is what makes its kill rule reachable.

7. ANY COLLECTION METHOD REQUIRING TOS VIOLATIONS OR PURCHASES (German Tank Checkout, Top-Mover Carousel) OR CONTRACTUALLY RESTRICTED DATA (Royalty Drip Nowcast, Fintech Vintage X-Ray). Not a cost question; a disqualification.

8. OUT OF CATALOG, FOR COMPLETENESS: the repo's own FTD 'Chronic-Fail Decay' result at /home/user/WireAntennaGain/research/ftd-empirical-findings.md should also not be funded as a short book on its own numbers — gross annualized 41-55% in the cheap bands sits squarely inside the hard-to-borrow fee range, and equal-weight shorting loses on the mean because 2.5% of observations squeeze more than +25%. It was not part of this catalog and has not been red-teamed; it should not be smuggled in as a forty-first playbook.

FUND AT APPROXIMATELY ZERO COST — INFRASTRUCTURE, NOT A POSITION: build and run the point-in-time FFIEC Call Report vintage archive (daily RetrieveFilersSubmissionDateTime poll plus RetrieveFacsimile snapshots, self-archived from day one). It costs a free registration, one endpoint and a cron job, and it captures the one genuinely unreconstructable asset in the whole catalog — as-filed vintages that no vendor or academic panel publishes and that are destroyed by overwrite. Its value is optionality, and it doubles as the amendment-contamination flag Test 1 needs. Attach no capital to its output and no expectation of a signal.

BUDGET AND GATES: research 1-2 weeks and <$500 now; capital $0 until Test 1's pre-registered criterion is met in full including all three robustness cuts and the placebo; if met, paper one quarter, then forward-test at 1/10 size for four quarters before any scaling; terminal sleeve cap 15% of book; hard stop at four consecutive quarters of negative rolling net spread. Do not re-specify the composite and re-run if Test 1 fails — that is the researcher-degrees-of-freedom failure the Dividend Clock Slip red team correctly identified as fatal at this event count.

PRE-SCREEN FOR THE NEXT BATCH — three questions that would have killed roughly 35 of these 40 in an hour, before any research spend: (a) Does a wire, an issuer press release, a regulator's own press room, or a commercial feed publish this first? (b) Are there at least 200 tradeable events per year, and can I therefore reject the null within five years? (c) Is there at least $2M/day of dollar volume, borrow under 3%, and a real instrument in the names where the signal actually fires — or does the signal only exist where liquidity does not? Failing any one of the three is a kill, not a research topic.
build_order: Week 0, day 1: Freeze the composite. Write the input list (RC-N 30-89 DPD by category, RI-B NCO and ALLL rebuild, RC-C CRE/C&D concentration; RC-O as control only; RI-E first-appearance lexicon), the winsorization, the z-scoring, the equal weights, and the go/no-go criterion into a signed, timestamped, version-controlled file. Do this BEFORE touching any return data. Nothing else in this list matters if this step is skipped.

Week 0, days 2-3: Build the ticker -> BHC -> lead-bank RSSD crosswalk from FFIEC NIC and FDIC BankFind, and apply the liquidity screen ($2M/day median dollar volume, price >= $5) to produce the ~130-180 name universe for each historical quarter point-in-time, so the backtest does not inherit today's survivors.

Week 0, days 3-5: Pull FFIEC/Chicago Fed Call Report bulk files 2010-2025 and extract the frozen fields, verifying MDRM codes against the live FFIEC 031/041/051 instructions and flagging every field-definition break introduced by the 2024-25 Call Report modernization.

Week 1, days 1-2: Pull EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02 acceptance timestamps and the FFIEC filing dates to classify every bank-quarter as CALL1 or CALL2. Report the CALL2 share; if it is materially below ~75% historically, the effect's carrier is weaker than BBE implies and the hurdle should be reconsidered before proceeding.
Week 1, day 3: Attach daily returns and build the KRE-hedged (or bank-peer-neutral) residual return series for t+1 to t+21 from each event date.

Week 1, days 4-5: Run Test 1 ONCE. Top-minus-bottom decile spread on CALL2 events, plus all three robustness cuts (2010-2017 vs 2018-2025; ex-2020Q1-Q2 and ex-2023Q1-Q2; dropping amended bank-quarters), plus the random-non-filing-day placebo, plus the leg-B RI-E lexicon test. Report every number, including the ones that fail.
Decision point: apply the kill rule literally. Spread < 40bp, or |t| < 3.0, or a sign flip in any robustness cut -> stop, write the negative result, delete the idea, do not re-specify and re-run.

In parallel from day 1, independent of the test outcome and at near-zero cost: stand up the point-in-time FFIEC vintage archive (registration, JWT with an 80-day rotation alarm, daily RetrieveFilersSubmissionDateTime poll, RetrieveFacsimile snapshots to immutable storage). It is infrastructure and an amendment-contamination flag, not a signal, and no capital is attached to it.
